scenes.setting: Britain. The garden of Cymbeline’s palace.

lines.text: Enter two Gentlemen.

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: You do not meet a man but frowns; our bloods

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: No more obey the heavens than our courtiers

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Still seem as does the King’s.

lines.speaker: SECOND GENTLEMAN
lines.text: But what’s the matter?

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: His daughter, and the heir of’s kingdom, whom

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: He purpos’d to his wife’s sole son—a widow

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: That late he married—hath referr’d herself

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Unto a poor but worthy gentleman. She’s wedded;

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Her husband banish’d; she imprison’d. All

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Is outward sorrow, though I think the King

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Be touch’d at very heart.

lines.speaker: SECOND GENTLEMAN
lines.text: None but the King?

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: He that hath lost her too. So is the Queen,

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: That most desir’d the match. But not a courtier,

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Although they wear their faces to the bent

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Of the King’s looks, hath a heart that is not

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Glad at the thing they scowl at.

lines.speaker: SECOND GENTLEMAN
lines.text: And why so?

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: He that hath miss’d the Princess is a thing

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Too bad for bad report; and he that hath her—

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: I mean that married her, alack, good man!

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: And therefore banish’d—is a creature such

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: As, to seek through the regions of the earth

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: For one his like, there would be something failing

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: In him that should compare. I do not think

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: So fair an outward and such stuff within

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Endows a man but he.

lines.speaker: SECOND GENTLEMAN
lines.text: You speak him far.

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: I do extend him, sir, within himself;

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Crush him together rather than unfold

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: His measure duly.

lines.speaker: SECOND GENTLEMAN
lines.text: What’s his name and birth?

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: I cannot delve him to the root; his father

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Was call’d Sicilius, who did join his honour

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Against the Romans with Cassibelan,

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: But had his titles by Tenantius, whom

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: He serv’d with glory and admir’d success,

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: So gain’d the sur-addition Leonatus;

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: And had, besides this gentleman in question,

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Two other sons, who, in the wars o’ th’ time,

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Died with their swords in hand; for which their father,

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Then old and fond of issue, took such sorrow

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: That he quit being; and his gentle lady,

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Big of this gentleman, our theme, deceas’d

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: As he was born. The King he takes the babe

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: To his protection, calls him Posthumus Leonatus,

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Breeds him and makes him of his bed-chamber,

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Puts to him all the learnings that his time

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Could make him the receiver of; which he took,

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: As we do air, fast as ’twas minist’red,

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: And in’s spring became a harvest, liv’d in court—

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Which rare it is to do—most prais’d, most lov’d,

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: A sample to the youngest; to th’ more mature

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: A glass that feated them; and to the graver

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: A child that guided dotards. To his mistress,

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: For whom he now is banish’d, her own price

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Proclaims how she esteem’d him and his virtue;

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: By her election may be truly read

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: What kind of man he is.

lines.speaker: SECOND GENTLEMAN
lines.text: I honour him

lines.speaker: SECOND GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Even out of your report. But pray you tell me,

lines.speaker: SECOND GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Is she sole child to th’ King?

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: His only child.

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: He had two sons—if this be worth your hearing,

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Mark it—the eldest of them at three years old,

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: I’ th’ swathing clothes the other, from their nursery

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Were stol’n; and to this hour no guess in knowledge

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Which way they went.

lines.speaker: SECOND GENTLEMAN
lines.text: How long is this ago?

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Some twenty years.

lines.speaker: SECOND GENTLEMAN
lines.text: That a king’s children should be so convey’d,

lines.speaker: SECOND GENTLEMAN
lines.text: So slackly guarded, and the search so slow

lines.speaker: SECOND GENTLEMAN
lines.text: That could not trace them!

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Howsoe’er ’tis strange,

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Or that the negligence may well be laugh’d at,

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Yet is it true, sir.

lines.speaker: SECOND GENTLEMAN
lines.text: I do well believe you.

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: We must forbear; here comes the gentleman,

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: The Queen, and Princess.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Queen, Posthumus and Imogen.

lines.text: No, be assur’d you shall not find me, daughter,

lines.text: After the slander of most stepmothers,

lines.text: Evil-ey’d unto you. You’re my prisoner, but

lines.text: Your gaoler shall deliver you the keys

lines.text: That lock up your restraint. For you, Posthumus,

lines.text: So soon as I can win th’ offended King,

lines.text: I will be known your advocate. Marry, yet

lines.text: The fire of rage is in him, and ’twere good

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: You lean’d unto his sentence with what patience

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Your wisdom may inform you.

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Please your Highness,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: I will from hence today.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: You know the peril.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: I’ll fetch a turn about the garden, pitying

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: The pangs of barr’d affections, though the King

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Hath charg’d you should not speak together.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: O dissembling courtesy! How fine this tyrant

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Can tickle where she wounds! My dearest husband,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: I something fear my father’s wrath, but nothing

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: (Always reserv’d my holy duty) what

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: His rage can do on me. You must be gone;

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: And I shall here abide the hourly shot

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Of angry eyes, not comforted to live

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: But that there is this jewel in the world

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: That I may see again.

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: My queen! my mistress!

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: O lady, weep no more, lest I give cause

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: To be suspected of more tenderness

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Than doth become a man. I will remain

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: The loyal’st husband that did e’er plight troth;

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: My residence in Rome at one Philario’s,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Who to my father was a friend, to me

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Known but by letter; thither write, my queen,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: And with mine eyes I’ll drink the words you send,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Though ink be made of gall.
Enter Queen.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Be brief, I pray you.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: If the King come, I shall incur I know not

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: How much of his displeasure. [_Aside._] Yet I’ll move him

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: To walk this way. I never do him wrong

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: But he does buy my injuries, to be friends;

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Pays dear for my offences.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Should we be taking leave

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: As long a term as yet we have to live,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: The loathness to depart would grow. Adieu!

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Nay, stay a little.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Were you but riding forth to air yourself,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Such parting were too petty. Look here, love:

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: This diamond was my mother’s; take it, heart;

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: But keep it till you woo another wife,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: When Imogen is dead.

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: How, how? Another?

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: You gentle gods, give me but this I have,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: And sear up my embracements from a next

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: With bonds of death! Remain, remain thou here
[_Puts on the ring._]

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: While sense can keep it on. And, sweetest, fairest,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: As I my poor self did exchange for you,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: To your so infinite loss, so in our trifles

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: I still win of you. For my sake wear this;

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: It is a manacle of love; I’ll place it

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Upon this fairest prisoner.
[_Puts a bracelet on her arm._]

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: O the gods!

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: When shall we see again?
Enter Cymbeline and Lords.

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Alack, the King!

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Thou basest thing, avoid; hence from my sight

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: If after this command thou fraught the court

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: With thy unworthiness, thou diest. Away!

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Thou’rt poison to my blood.

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: The gods protect you,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: And bless the good remainders of the court!

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: I am gone.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: There cannot be a pinch in death

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: More sharp than this is.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: O disloyal thing,

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: That shouldst repair my youth, thou heap’st

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: A year’s age on me!

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: I beseech you, sir,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Harm not yourself with your vexation.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: I am senseless of your wrath; a touch more rare

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Subdues all pangs, all fears.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Past grace? obedience?

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Past hope, and in despair; that way past grace.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: That mightst have had the sole son of my queen!

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: O blessed that I might not! I chose an eagle,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: And did avoid a puttock.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Thou took’st a beggar, wouldst have made my throne

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: A seat for baseness.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: No; I rather added

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: A lustre to it.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: O thou vile one!

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Sir,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: It is your fault that I have lov’d Posthumus.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: You bred him as my playfellow, and he is

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: A man worth any woman; overbuys me

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Almost the sum he pays.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: What, art thou mad?

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Almost, sir. Heaven restore me! Would I were

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: A neat-herd’s daughter, and my Leonatus

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Our neighbour shepherd’s son!
Enter Queen.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Thou foolish thing!
[_To the Queen._]

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: They were again together. You have done

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Not after our command. Away with her,

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: And pen her up.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Beseech your patience. Peace,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Dear lady daughter, peace!—Sweet sovereign,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Leave us to ourselves, and make yourself some comfort

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Out of your best advice.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Nay, let her languish

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: A drop of blood a day and, being aged,

lines.text: Die of this folly.
[_Exit with Lords._]
Enter Pisanio.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Fie! you must give way.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Here is your servant. How now, sir! What news?

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: My lord your son drew on my master.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Ha!

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: No harm, I trust, is done?

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: There might have been,

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: But that my master rather play’d than fought,

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: And had no help of anger; they were parted

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: By gentlemen at hand.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: I am very glad on’t.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Your son’s my father’s friend; he takes his part

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: To draw upon an exile! O brave sir!

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: I would they were in Afric both together;

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Myself by with a needle, that I might prick

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: The goer-back. Why came you from your master?

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: On his command. He would not suffer me

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: To bring him to the haven; left these notes

lines.text: Of what commands I should be subject to,

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: When’t pleas’d you to employ me.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: This hath been

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Your faithful servant. I dare lay mine honour

lines.text: He will remain so.

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: I humbly thank your Highness.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Pray walk awhile.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: About some half-hour hence,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Pray you speak with me.

lines.text: You shall at least go see my lord aboard.

lines.text: For this time leave me.

Enter Cloten and two Lords.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Sir, I would advise you to shift a shirt; the violence of action hath

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: made you reek as a sacrifice. Where air comes out, air comes in;

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: there’s none abroad so wholesome as that you vent.

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: If my shirt were bloody, then to shift it. Have I hurt him?
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: No, faith; not so much as his patience.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Hurt him! His body’s a passable carcass if he be not hurt. It is a

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: throughfare for steel if it be not hurt.
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: His steel was in debt; it went o’ th’ backside the town.

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: The villain would not stand me.
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: No; but he fled forward still, toward your face.

lines.text: Stand you? You have land enough of your own; but he added to your

lines.text: having, gave you some ground.
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD

lines.text: Puppies!

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: I would they had not come between us.
[_Aside._]

lines.text: So would I, till you had measur’d how long a fool you were

lines.text: upon the ground.

lines.text: And that she should love this fellow, and refuse me!
[_Aside._]

lines.text: If it be a sin to make a true election, she is damn’d.

lines.text: Sir, as I told you always, her beauty and her brain go not together;

lines.text: she’s a good sign, but I have seen small reflection of her wit.
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: She shines not upon fools, lest the reflection should hurt

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: her.

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Come, I’ll to my chamber. Would there had been some hurt done!
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: I wish not so; unless it had been the fall of an ass, which

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: is no great hurt.

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: You’ll go with us?

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: I’ll attend your lordship.

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Nay, come, let’s go together.

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: Well, my lord.

lines.text: What is the matter, trow?

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: The cloyed will—

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: That satiate yet unsatisfied desire, that tub

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Both fill’d and running—ravening first the lamb,

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Longs after for the garbage.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: What, dear sir,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Thus raps you? Are you well?

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Thanks, madam; well. Beseech you, sir,

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Desire my man’s abode where I did leave him.

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: He’s strange and peevish.

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: I was going, sir,

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: To give him welcome.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Continues well my lord? His health beseech you?

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Well, madam.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Is he dispos’d to mirth? I hope he is.

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Exceeding pleasant; none a stranger there

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: So merry and so gamesome. He is call’d

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: The Briton reveller.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: When he was here

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: He did incline to sadness, and oft-times

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Not knowing why.

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: I never saw him sad.

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: There is a Frenchman his companion, one

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: An eminent monsieur that, it seems, much loves

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: A Gallian girl at home. He furnaces

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: The thick sighs from him; whiles the jolly Briton

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: (Your lord, I mean) laughs from’s free lungs, cries “O,

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Can my sides hold, to think that man, who knows

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: By history, report, or his own proof,

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: What woman is, yea, what she cannot choose

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: But must be, will’s free hours languish for

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Assured bondage?”

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Will my lord say so?

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Ay, madam, with his eyes in flood with laughter.

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: It is a recreation to be by

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: And hear him mock the Frenchman. But heavens know

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Some men are much to blame.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Not he, I hope.

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Not he; but yet heaven’s bounty towards him might

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Be us’d more thankfully. In himself, ’tis much;

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: In you, which I account his, beyond all talents.

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Whilst I am bound to wonder, I am bound

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: To pity too.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: What do you pity, sir?

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Two creatures heartily.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Am I one, sir?

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: You look on me: what wreck discern you in me

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Deserves your pity?

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Lamentable! What,

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: To hide me from the radiant sun and solace

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: I’ th’ dungeon by a snuff?

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: I pray you, sir,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Deliver with more openness your answers

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: To my demands. Why do you pity me?

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: That others do,

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: I was about to say, enjoy your—But

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: It is an office of the gods to venge it,

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Not mine to speak on’t.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: You do seem to know

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Something of me, or what concerns me; pray you,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Since doubting things go ill often hurts more

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Than to be sure they do; for certainties

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Either are past remedies, or, timely knowing,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: The remedy then born—discover to me

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: What both you spur and stop.

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Had I this cheek

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: To bathe my lips upon; this hand, whose touch,

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Whose every touch, would force the feeler’s soul

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: To th’ oath of loyalty; this object, which

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Takes prisoner the wild motion of mine eye,

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Fixing it only here; should I, damn’d then,

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Slaver with lips as common as the stairs

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: That mount the Capitol; join gripes with hands

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Made hard with hourly falsehood (falsehood as

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: With labour): then by-peeping in an eye

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Base and illustrious as the smoky light

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: That’s fed with stinking tallow: it were fit

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: That all the plagues of hell should at one time

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Encounter such revolt.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: My lord, I fear,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Has forgot Britain.

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: And himself. Not I

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Inclin’d to this intelligence pronounce

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: The beggary of his change; but ’tis your graces

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: That from my mutest conscience to my tongue

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Charms this report out.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Let me hear no more.

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: O dearest soul, your cause doth strike my heart

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: With pity that doth make me sick! A lady

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: So fair, and fasten’d to an empery,

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Would make the great’st king double, to be partner’d

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: With tomboys hir’d with that self exhibition

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Which your own coffers yield! with diseas’d ventures

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: That play with all infirmities for gold

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Which rottenness can lend nature! Such boil’d stuff

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: As well might poison poison! Be reveng’d;

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Or she that bore you was no queen, and you

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Recoil from your great stock.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Reveng’d?

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: How should I be reveng’d? If this be true,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: (As I have such a heart that both mine ears

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Must not in haste abuse) if it be true,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: How should I be reveng’d?

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Should he make me

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Live like Diana’s priest betwixt cold sheets,

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Whiles he is vaulting variable ramps,

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: In your despite, upon your purse? Revenge it.

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: I dedicate myself to your sweet pleasure,

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: More noble than that runagate to your bed,

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: And will continue fast to your affection,

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Still close as sure.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: What ho, Pisanio!

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Let me my service tender on your lips.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Away! I do condemn mine ears that have

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: So long attended thee. If thou wert honourable,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Thou wouldst have told this tale for virtue, not

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: For such an end thou seek’st, as base as strange.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Thou wrong’st a gentleman who is as far

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: From thy report as thou from honour; and

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Solicits here a lady that disdains

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Thee and the devil alike. What ho, Pisanio!

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: The King my father shall be made acquainted

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Of thy assault. If he shall think it fit

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: A saucy stranger in his court to mart

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: As in a Romish stew, and to expound

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: His beastly mind to us, he hath a court

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: He little cares for, and a daughter who

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: He not respects at all. What ho, Pisanio!

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: O happy Leonatus! I may say

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: The credit that thy lady hath of thee

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Deserves thy trust, and thy most perfect goodness

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Her assur’d credit. Blessed live you long,

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: A lady to the worthiest sir that ever

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Country call’d his! and you his mistress, only

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: For the most worthiest fit! Give me your pardon.

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: I have spoke this to know if your affiance

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Were deeply rooted, and shall make your lord

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: That which he is new o’er; and he is one

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: The truest manner’d, such a holy witch

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: That he enchants societies into him,

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Half all men’s hearts are his.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: You make amends.

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: He sits ’mongst men like a descended god:

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: He hath a kind of honour sets him off

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: More than a mortal seeming. Be not angry,

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Most mighty Princess, that I have adventur’d

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: To try your taking of a false report, which hath

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Honour’d with confirmation your great judgement

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: In the election of a sir so rare,

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Which you know cannot err. The love I bear him

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Made me to fan you thus; but the gods made you,

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Unlike all others, chaffless. Pray your pardon.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: All’s well, sir; take my pow’r i’ th’ court for yours.

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: My humble thanks. I had almost forgot

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: T’ entreat your Grace but in a small request,

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: And yet of moment too, for it concerns

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Your lord; myself and other noble friends

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Are partners in the business.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Pray what is’t?

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Some dozen Romans of us, and your lord

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: (The best feather of our wing) have mingled sums

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: To buy a present for the Emperor;

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Which I, the factor for the rest, have done

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: In France. ’Tis plate of rare device, and jewels

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Of rich and exquisite form, their values great;

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: And I am something curious, being strange,

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: To have them in safe stowage. May it please you

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: To take them in protection?

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Willingly;

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: And pawn mine honour for their safety. Since

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: My lord hath interest in them, I will keep them

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: In my bedchamber.

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: They are in a trunk,

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Attended by my men. I will make bold

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: To send them to you only for this night;

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: I must aboard tomorrow.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: O, no, no.

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Yes, I beseech; or I shall short my word

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: By length’ning my return. From Gallia

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: I cross’d the seas on purpose and on promise

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: To see your Grace.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: I thank you for your pains.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: But not away tomorrow!

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: O, I must, madam.

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Therefore I shall beseech you, if you please

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: To greet your lord with writing, do’t tonight.

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: I have outstood my time, which is material

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: To th’ tender of our present.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: I will write.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Send your trunk to me; it shall safe be kept

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: And truly yielded you. You’re very welcome.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Cloten and the two Lords.

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Was there ever man had such luck! When I kiss’d the jack, upon an

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: upcast to be hit away! I had a hundred pound on’t; and then a whoreson

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: jackanapes must take me up for swearing, as if I borrowed mine oaths of

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: him, and might not spend them at my pleasure.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: What got he by that? You have broke his pate with your bowl.
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: If his wit had been like him that broke it, it would have

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: run all out.

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: When a gentleman is dispos’d to swear, it is not for any standers-by to

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: curtail his oaths. Ha?

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: No, my lord; [_Aside._] nor crop the ears of them.

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Whoreson dog! I gave him satisfaction. Would he had been one of my

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: rank!
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: To have smell’d like a fool.

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: I am not vex’d more at anything in th’ earth. A pox on’t! I had rather

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: not be so noble as I am; they dare not fight with me, because of the

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Queen my mother. Every jackslave hath his bellyful of fighting, and I

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: must go up and down like a cock that nobody can match.
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: You are cock and capon too; and you crow, cock, with your

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: comb on.

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Sayest thou?

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: It is not fit your lordship should undertake every companion that you

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: give offence to.

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: No, I know that; but it is fit I should commit offence to my inferiors.

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: Ay, it is fit for your lordship only.

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Why, so I say.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Did you hear of a stranger that’s come to court tonight?

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: A stranger, and I not known on’t?
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: He’s a strange fellow himself, and knows it not.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: There’s an Italian come, and, ’tis thought, one of Leonatus’ friends.

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Leonatus? A banish’d rascal; and he’s another, whatsoever he be. Who

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: told you of this stranger?

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: One of your lordship’s pages.

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Is it fit I went to look upon him? Is there no derogation in’t?

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: You cannot derogate, my lord.

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Not easily, I think.
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: You are a fool granted; therefore your issues, being

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: foolish, do not derogate.

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Come, I’ll go see this Italian. What I have lost today at bowls I’ll

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: win tonight of him. Come, go.

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: I’ll attend your lordship.
[_Exeunt Cloten and First Lord._]

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: That such a crafty devil as is his mother

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: Should yield the world this ass! A woman that

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: Bears all down with her brain; and this her son

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: Cannot take two from twenty, for his heart,

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: And leave eighteen. Alas, poor princess,

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: Thou divine Imogen, what thou endur’st,

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: Betwixt a father by thy step-dame govern’d,

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: A mother hourly coining plots, a wooer

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: More hateful than the foul expulsion is

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: Of thy dear husband, than that horrid act

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: Of the divorce he’d make! The heavens hold firm

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: The walls of thy dear honour, keep unshak’d

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: That temple, thy fair mind, that thou mayst stand

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: T’ enjoy thy banish’d lord and this great land!
[_Exit._]

scenes.setting: Britain. Imogen’s bedchamber in Cymbeline’s palace; a trunk

lines.text: in one corner.
Enter Imogen in her bed, and a Lady attending.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Who’s there? My woman Helen?

lines.speaker: LADY
lines.text: Please you, madam.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: What hour is it?

lines.speaker: LADY
lines.text: Almost midnight, madam.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: I have read three hours then. Mine eyes are weak;

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Fold down the leaf where I have left. To bed.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Take not away the taper, leave it burning;

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: And if thou canst awake by four o’ th’ clock,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: I prithee call me. Sleep hath seiz’d me wholly.
[_Exit Lady._]

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: To your protection I commend me, gods.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: From fairies and the tempters of the night

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Guard me, beseech ye!
[_Sleeps. Iachimo comes from the trunk._]

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: The crickets sing, and man’s o’er-labour’d sense

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Repairs itself by rest. Our Tarquin thus

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Did softly press the rushes ere he waken’d

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: The chastity he wounded. Cytherea,

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: How bravely thou becom’st thy bed! fresh lily,

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: And whiter than the sheets! That I might touch!

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: But kiss; one kiss! Rubies unparagon’d,

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: How dearly they do’t! ’Tis her breathing that

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Perfumes the chamber thus. The flame o’ th’ taper

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Bows toward her and would under-peep her lids

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: To see th’ enclosed lights, now canopied

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Under these windows white and azure, lac’d

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: With blue of heaven’s own tinct. But my design

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: To note the chamber. I will write all down:

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Such and such pictures; there the window; such

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Th’ adornment of her bed; the arras, figures,

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Why, such and such; and the contents o’ th’ story.

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Ah, but some natural notes about her body

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Above ten thousand meaner movables

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Would testify, t’ enrich mine inventory.

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: O sleep, thou ape of death, lie dull upon her!

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: And be her sense but as a monument,

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Thus in a chapel lying! Come off, come off;
[_Taking off her bracelet._]

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: As slippery as the Gordian knot was hard!

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: ’Tis mine; and this will witness outwardly,

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: As strongly as the conscience does within,

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: To th’ madding of her lord. On her left breast

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: A mole cinque-spotted, like the crimson drops

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: I’ th’ bottom of a cowslip. Here’s a voucher

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Stronger than ever law could make; this secret

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Will force him think I have pick’d the lock and ta’en

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: The treasure of her honour. No more. To what end?

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Why should I write this down that’s riveted,

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Screw’d to my memory? She hath been reading late

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: The tale of Tereus; here the leaf’s turn’d down

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Where Philomel gave up. I have enough.

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: To th’ trunk again, and shut the spring of it.

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Swift, swift, you dragons of the night, that dawning

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: May bare the raven’s eye! I lodge in fear;

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Though this a heavenly angel, hell is here.
[_Clock strikes._]

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: One, two, three. Time, time!
[_Exit into the trunk._]

scenes.setting: Cymbeline’s palace. An ante-chamber adjoining Imogen’s

lines.text: apartments.
Enter Cloten and Lords.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Your lordship is the most patient man in loss, the most coldest that

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: ever turn’d up ace.

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: It would make any man cold to lose.

lines.speaker: PHILARIO
lines.text: And take your ring again; ’tis not yet won.

lines.speaker: PHILARIO
lines.text: It may be probable she lost it, or

lines.speaker: PHILARIO
lines.text: Who knows if one her women, being corrupted

lines.speaker: PHILARIO
lines.text: Hath stol’n it from her?

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Very true;

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: And so I hope he came by’t. Back my ring.

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Render to me some corporal sign about her,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: More evident than this; for this was stol’n.

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: By Jupiter, I had it from her arm!

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Hark you, he swears; by Jupiter he swears.

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: ’Tis true, nay, keep the ring, ’tis true. I am sure

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: She would not lose it. Her attendants are

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: All sworn and honourable:—they induc’d to steal it!

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: And by a stranger! No, he hath enjoy’d her.

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: The cognizance of her incontinency

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Is this: she hath bought the name of whore thus dearly.

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: There, take thy hire; and all the fiends of hell

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Divide themselves between you!

lines.speaker: PHILARIO
lines.text: Sir, be patient;

lines.speaker: PHILARIO
lines.text: This is not strong enough to be believ’d

lines.speaker: PHILARIO
lines.text: Of one persuaded well of.

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Never talk on’t;

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: She hath been colted by him.

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: If you seek

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: For further satisfying, under her breast

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: (Worthy the pressing) lies a mole, right proud

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Of that most delicate lodging. By my life,

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: I kiss’d it; and it gave me present hunger

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: To feed again, though full. You do remember

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: This stain upon her?

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Ay, and it doth confirm

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Another stain, as big as hell can hold,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Were there no more but it.

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Will you hear more?

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Spare your arithmetic; never count the turns.

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Once, and a million!

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: I’ll be sworn—

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: No swearing.

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: If you will swear you have not done’t, you lie;

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: And I will kill thee if thou dost deny

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Thou’st made me cuckold.

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: I’ll deny nothing.

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: O that I had her here to tear her limb-meal!

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: I will go there and do’t, i’ th’ court, before

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Her father. I’ll do something—
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: PHILARIO
lines.text: Quite besides

lines.speaker: PHILARIO
lines.text: The government of patience! You have won.

lines.speaker: PHILARIO
lines.text: Let’s follow him and pervert the present wrath

lines.speaker: PHILARIO

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: With all my heart.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: Rome. Another room in Philario’s house.

lines.text: Enter Posthumus.

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Is there no way for men to be, but women

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Must be half-workers? We are all bastards,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: And that most venerable man which I

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Did call my father was I know not where

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: When I was stamp’d. Some coiner with his tools

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Made me a counterfeit; yet my mother seem’d

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: The Dian of that time. So doth my wife

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: The nonpareil of this. O, vengeance, vengeance!

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Me of my lawful pleasure she restrain’d,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: And pray’d me oft forbearance; did it with

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: A pudency so rosy, the sweet view on’t

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Might well have warm’d old Saturn; that I thought her

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: As chaste as unsunn’d snow. O, all the devils!

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: This yellow Iachimo in an hour, was’t not?

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Or less; at first? Perchance he spoke not, but,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Like a full-acorn’d boar, a German one,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Cried “O!” and mounted; found no opposition

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: But what he look’d for should oppose and she

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Should from encounter guard. Could I find out

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: The woman’s part in me! For there’s no motion

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: That tends to vice in man but I affirm

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: It is the woman’s part. Be it lying, note it,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: The woman’s; flattering, hers; deceiving, hers;

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Lust and rank thoughts, hers, hers; revenges, hers;

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Ambitions, covetings, change of prides, disdain,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Nice longing, slanders, mutability,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: All faults that man may name, nay, that hell knows,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Why, hers, in part or all; but rather all;

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: For even to vice

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: They are not constant, but are changing still

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: One vice but of a minute old for one

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Not half so old as that. I’ll write against them,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Detest them, curse them. Yet ’tis greater skill

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: In a true hate to pray they have their will:

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: The very devils cannot plague them better.
[_Exit._]

scenes.setting: Britain. A hall in Cymbeline’s palace.

lines.text: Enter in state Cymbeline, Queen, Cloten and Lords at one door, and at another Caius Lucius and Attendants.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Now say, what would Augustus Cæsar with us?

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: When Julius Cæsar, (whose remembrance yet

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Lives in men’s eyes, and will to ears and tongues

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Be theme and hearing ever) was in this Britain,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: And conquer’d it, Cassibelan, thine uncle,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Famous in Cæsar’s praises no whit less

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Than in his feats deserving it, for him

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: And his succession granted Rome a tribute,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Yearly three thousand pounds, which by thee lately

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Is left untender’d.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: And, to kill the marvel,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Shall be so ever.

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: There be many Cæsars ere such another Julius. Britain is a world by

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: itself, and we will nothing pay for wearing our own noses.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: That opportunity,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Which then they had to take from’s, to resume

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: We have again. Remember, sir, my liege,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: The kings your ancestors, together with

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: The natural bravery of your isle, which stands

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: As Neptune’s park, ribb’d and pal’d in

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: With rocks unscaleable and roaring waters,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: With sands that will not bear your enemies’ boats

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: But suck them up to th’ top-mast. A kind of conquest

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Cæsar made here, but made not here his brag

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Of ‘Came, and saw, and overcame.’ With shame

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: (The first that ever touch’d him) he was carried

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: From off our coast, twice beaten; and his shipping

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: (Poor ignorant baubles!) on our terrible seas,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Like egg-shells mov’d upon their surges, crack’d

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: As easily ’gainst our rocks; for joy whereof

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: The fam’d Cassibelan, who was once at point

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: (O, giglot fortune!) to master Cæsar’s sword,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Made Lud’s Town with rejoicing fires bright

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: And Britons strut with courage.

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Come, there’s no more tribute to be paid. Our kingdom is stronger than

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: it was at that time; and, as I said, there is no moe such Cæsars. Other

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: of them may have crook’d noses; but to owe such straight arms, none.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Son, let your mother end.

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: We have yet many among us can gripe as hard as Cassibelan. I do not say

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: I am one; but I have a hand. Why tribute? Why should we pay tribute? If

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Cæsar can hide the sun from us with a blanket, or put the moon in his

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: pocket, we will pay him tribute for light; else, sir, no more tribute,

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: pray you now.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: You must know,

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Till the injurious Romans did extort

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: This tribute from us, we were free. Cæsar’s ambition,

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Which swell’d so much that it did almost stretch

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: The sides o’ th’ world, against all colour here

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Did put the yoke upon’s; which to shake off

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Becomes a warlike people, whom we reckon

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Ourselves to be.

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: We do.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Say then to Cæsar,

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Our ancestor was that Mulmutius which

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Ordain’d our laws, whose use the sword of Cæsar

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Hath too much mangled; whose repair and franchise

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Shall, by the power we hold, be our good deed,

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Though Rome be therefore angry. Mulmutius made our laws,

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Who was the first of Britain which did put

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: His brows within a golden crown, and call’d

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Himself a king.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: I am sorry, Cymbeline,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: That I am to pronounce Augustus Cæsar

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: (Cæsar, that hath moe kings his servants than

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Thyself domestic officers) thine enemy.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Receive it from me, then: war and confusion

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: In Cæsar’s name pronounce I ’gainst thee; look

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: For fury not to be resisted. Thus defied,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: I thank thee for myself.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Thou art welcome, Caius.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Thy Cæsar knighted me; my youth I spent

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Much under him; of him I gather’d honour,

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Which he to seek of me again, perforce,

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Behoves me keep at utterance. I am perfect

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: That the Pannonians and Dalmatians for

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Their liberties are now in arms, a precedent

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Which not to read would show the Britons cold;

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: So Cæsar shall not find them.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Let proof speak.

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: His majesty bids you welcome. Make pastime with us a day or two, or

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: longer. If you seek us afterwards in other terms, you shall find us in

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: our salt-water girdle. If you beat us out of it, it is yours; if you

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: fall in the adventure, our crows shall fare the better for you; and

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: there’s an end.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: So, sir.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: I know your master’s pleasure, and he mine;

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: All the remain is, welcome.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: Britain. Another room in Cymbeline’s palace.

lines.text: Enter Pisanio reading of a letter.

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: How? of adultery? Wherefore write you not

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: What monsters her accuse? Leonatus!

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: O master, what a strange infection

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: Is fall’n into thy ear! What false Italian

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: (As poisonous-tongu’d as handed) hath prevail’d

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: On thy too ready hearing? Disloyal? No.

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: She’s punish’d for her truth, and undergoes,

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: More goddess-like than wife-like, such assaults

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: As would take in some virtue. O my master,

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: Thy mind to her is now as low as were

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: Thy fortunes. How? that I should murder her?

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: Upon the love, and truth, and vows, which I

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: Have made to thy command? I, her? Her blood?

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: If it be so to do good service, never

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: Let me be counted serviceable. How look I

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: That I should seem to lack humanity

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: So much as this fact comes to?
[_Reads._]

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: ‘Do’t. The letter

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: That I have sent her, by her own command

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: Shall give thee opportunity.’ O damn’d paper,

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: Black as the ink that’s on thee! Senseless bauble,

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: Art thou a fedary for this act, and look’st

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: So virgin-like without? Lo, here she comes.
Enter Imogen.

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: I am ignorant in what I am commanded.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: How now, Pisanio?

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: Madam, here is a letter from my lord.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Who? thy lord? That is my lord, Leonatus?

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: O, learn’d indeed were that astronomer

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: That knew the stars as I his characters;

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: He’d lay the future open. You good gods,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Let what is here contain’d relish of love,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Of my lord’s health, of his content; yet not

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: That we two are asunder; let that grieve him!

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Some griefs are med’cinable; that is one of them,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: For it doth physic love: of his content,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: All but in that. Good wax, thy leave. Blest be

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: You bees that make these locks of counsel! Lovers

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: And men in dangerous bonds pray not alike;

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Though forfeiters you cast in prison, yet

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: You clasp young Cupid’s tables. Good news, gods!
[_Reads._]

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: _Justice and your father’s wrath, should he take me in his dominion,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: could not be so cruel to me as you, O the dearest of creatures, would

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: even renew me with your eyes. Take notice that I am in Cambria, at

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Milford Haven. What your own love will out of this advise you, follow.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: So he wishes you all happiness that remains loyal to his vow, and your

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: increasing in love.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: LEONATUS POSTHUMUS._

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: O for a horse with wings! Hear’st thou, Pisanio?

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: He is at Milford Haven. Read, and tell me

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: How far ’tis thither. If one of mean affairs

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: May plod it in a week, why may not I

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Glide thither in a day? Then, true Pisanio,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Who long’st like me to see thy lord, who long’st

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: (O, let me ’bate!) but not like me, yet long’st,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: But in a fainter kind. O, not like me,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: For mine’s beyond beyond: say, and speak thick,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: (Love’s counsellor should fill the bores of hearing

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: To th’ smothering of the sense) how far it is

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: To this same blessed Milford. And by th’ way

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Tell me how Wales was made so happy as

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: T’ inherit such a haven. But first of all,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: How we may steal from hence; and for the gap

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: That we shall make in time from our hence-going

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: And our return, to excuse. But first, how get hence.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Why should excuse be born or ere begot?

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: We’ll talk of that hereafter. Prithee speak,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: How many score of miles may we well rid

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: ’Twixt hour and hour?

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: One score ’twixt sun and sun,

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: Madam, ’s enough for you, and too much too.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Why, one that rode to’s execution, man,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Could never go so slow. I have heard of riding wagers

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Where horses have been nimbler than the sands

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: That run i’ th’ clock’s behalf. But this is fool’ry.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Go bid my woman feign a sickness; say

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: She’ll home to her father; and provide me presently

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: A riding suit, no costlier than would fit

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: A franklin’s huswife.

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: Madam, you’re best consider.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: I see before me, man. Nor here, nor here,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Nor what ensues, but have a fog in them

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: That I cannot look through. Away, I prithee;

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Do as I bid thee. There’s no more to say.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Accessible is none but Milford way.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: Wales. A mountainous country with a cave.

lines.text: Enter from the cave Belarius, Guiderius and Arviragus.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: A goodly day not to keep house with such

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Whose roof’s as low as ours! Stoop, boys; this gate

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Instructs you how t’ adore the heavens, and bows you

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: To a morning’s holy office. The gates of monarchs

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Are arch’d so high that giants may jet through

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: And keep their impious turbans on without

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Good morrow to the sun. Hail, thou fair heaven!

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: We house i’ th’ rock, yet use thee not so hardly

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: As prouder livers do.

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Hail, heaven!

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: Hail, heaven!

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Now for our mountain sport. Up to yond hill,

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Your legs are young; I’ll tread these flats. Consider,

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: When you above perceive me like a crow,

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: That it is place which lessens and sets off;

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: And you may then revolve what tales I have told you

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Of courts, of princes, of the tricks in war.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: This service is not service so being done,

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: But being so allow’d. To apprehend thus

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Draws us a profit from all things we see,

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: And often to our comfort shall we find

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: The sharded beetle in a safer hold

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Than is the full-wing’d eagle. O, this life

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Is nobler than attending for a check,

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Richer than doing nothing for a robe,

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Prouder than rustling in unpaid-for silk:

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Such gain the cap of him that makes him fine,

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Yet keeps his book uncross’d. No life to ours!

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Out of your proof you speak. We, poor unfledg’d,

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS

lines.text: And fit you to your manhood. May the gods

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: Direct you to the best!

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Amen. I thank thee.
[_Exeunt severally._]
Enter Cymbeline, Queen, Cloten, Lucius and Lords.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Thus far, and so farewell.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Thanks, royal sir.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: My emperor hath wrote; I must from hence,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: And am right sorry that I must report ye

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: My master’s enemy.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Our subjects, sir,

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Will not endure his yoke; and for ourself

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: To show less sovereignty than they, must needs

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Appear unkinglike.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: So, sir. I desire of you

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: A conduct overland to Milford Haven.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Madam, all joy befall your Grace, and you!

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: My lords, you are appointed for that office;

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: The due of honour in no point omit.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: So farewell, noble Lucius.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Your hand, my lord.

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Receive it friendly; but from this time forth

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: I wear it as your enemy.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Sir, the event

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Is yet to name the winner. Fare you well.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Leave not the worthy Lucius, good my lords,

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Till he have cross’d the Severn. Happiness!
[_Exeunt Lucius and Lords._]

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: He goes hence frowning; but it honours us

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: That we have given him cause.

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: ’Tis all the better;

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Your valiant Britons have their wishes in it.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Lucius hath wrote already to the Emperor

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: How it goes here. It fits us therefore ripely

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Our chariots and our horsemen be in readiness.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: The pow’rs that he already hath in Gallia

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Will soon be drawn to head, from whence he moves

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: His war for Britain.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: ’Tis not sleepy business,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: But must be look’d to speedily and strongly.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Our expectation that it would be thus

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Hath made us forward. But, my gentle queen,

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Where is our daughter? She hath not appear’d

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Before the Roman, nor to us hath tender’d

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: The duty of the day. She looks us like

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: A thing more made of malice than of duty;

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: We have noted it. Call her before us, for

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: We have been too slight in sufferance.
[_Exit an Attendant._]

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Royal sir,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Since the exile of Posthumus, most retir’d

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Hath her life been; the cure whereof, my lord,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: ’Tis time must do. Beseech your Majesty,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Forbear sharp speeches to her; she’s a lady

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: So tender of rebukes that words are strokes,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: And strokes death to her.
Enter Attendant.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Where is she, sir? How

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Can her contempt be answer’d?

lines.speaker: ATTENDANT
lines.text: Please you, sir,

lines.speaker: ATTENDANT
lines.text: Her chambers are all lock’d, and there’s no answer

lines.speaker: ATTENDANT
lines.text: That will be given to th’ loud of noise we make.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: My lord, when last I went to visit her,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: She pray’d me to excuse her keeping close;

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Whereto constrain’d by her infirmity

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: She should that duty leave unpaid to you

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Which daily she was bound to proffer. This

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: She wish’d me to make known; but our great court

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Made me to blame in memory.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Her doors lock’d?

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Not seen of late? Grant, heavens, that which I fear

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Prove false!
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Son, I say, follow the King.

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: That man of hers, Pisanio, her old servant,

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: I have not seen these two days.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Go, look after.
[_Exit Cloten._]

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Pisanio, thou that stand’st so for Posthumus!

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: He hath a drug of mine. I pray his absence

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Proceed by swallowing that; for he believes

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: It is a thing most precious. But for her,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Where is she gone? Haply despair hath seiz’d her;

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Or, wing’d with fervour of her love, she’s flown

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: To her desir’d Posthumus. Gone she is

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: To death or to dishonour, and my end

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Can make good use of either. She being down,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: I have the placing of the British crown.
Enter Cloten.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: How now, my son?

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: ’Tis certain she is fled.

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Go in and cheer the King. He rages; none

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Dare come about him.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: All the better. May

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: This night forestall him of the coming day!
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: I love and hate her; for she’s fair and royal,

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: And that she hath all courtly parts more exquisite

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Than lady, ladies, woman. From every one

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: The best she hath, and she, of all compounded,

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Outsells them all. I love her therefore; but

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Disdaining me and throwing favours on

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: The low Posthumus slanders so her judgement

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: That what’s else rare is chok’d; and in that point

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: I will conclude to hate her, nay, indeed,

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: To be reveng’d upon her. For when fools

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Shall—
Enter Pisanio.

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Who is here? What, are you packing, sirrah?

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Come hither. Ah, you precious pandar! Villain,

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Where is thy lady? In a word, or else

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Thou art straightway with the fiends.

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: O good my lord!

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Where is thy lady? or, by Jupiter—

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: I will not ask again. Close villain,

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: I’ll have this secret from thy heart, or rip

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Thy heart to find it. Is she with Posthumus?

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: From whose so many weights of baseness cannot

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: A dram of worth be drawn.

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: Alas, my lord,

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: How can she be with him? When was she miss’d?

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: He is in Rome.

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Where is she, sir? Come nearer.

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: No farther halting! Satisfy me home

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: What is become of her.

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: O my all-worthy lord!

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: All-worthy villain!

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Discover where thy mistress is at once,

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: At the next word. No more of ‘worthy lord’!

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Speak, or thy silence on the instant is

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Thy condemnation and thy death.

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: Then, sir,

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: This paper is the history of my knowledge

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: Touching her flight.
[_Presenting a letter._]

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Let’s see’t. I will pursue her

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Even to Augustus’ throne.
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: Or this or perish.

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: She’s far enough; and what he learns by this

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: May prove his travel, not her danger.

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Humh!
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: I’ll write to my lord she’s dead. O Imogen,

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: Safe mayst thou wander, safe return again!

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Sirrah, is this letter true?

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: Sir, as I think.

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: It is Posthumus’ hand; I know’t. Sirrah, if thou wouldst not be a

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: villain, but do me true service, undergo those employments wherein I

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: should have cause to use thee with a serious industry—that is, what

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: villainy soe’er I bid thee do, to perform it directly and truly—I would

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: think thee an honest man; thou shouldst neither want my means for thy

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: relief nor my voice for thy preferment.

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: Well, my good lord.

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Wilt thou serve me? For since patiently and constantly thou hast stuck

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: to the bare fortune of that beggar Posthumus, thou canst not, in the

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: course of gratitude, but be a diligent follower of mine. Wilt thou

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: serve me?

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: Sir, I will.

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Give me thy hand; here’s my purse. Hast any of thy late master’s

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: garments in thy possession?

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: I have, my lord, at my lodging, the same suit he wore when he took

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: leave of my lady and mistress.

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: The first service thou dost me, fetch that suit hither. Let it be thy

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: first service; go.

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: I shall, my lord.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Meet thee at Milford Haven! I forgot to ask him one thing; I’ll

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: remember’t anon. Even there, thou villain Posthumus, will I kill thee.

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: I would these garments were come. She said upon a time—the bitterness

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: of it I now belch from my heart—that she held the very garment of

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Posthumus in more respect than my noble and natural person, together

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: with the adornment of my qualities. With that suit upon my back will I

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: ravish her; first kill him, and in her eyes. There shall she see my

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: valour, which will then be a torment to her contempt. He on the ground,

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: my speech of insultment ended on his dead body, and when my lust hath

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: dined—which, as I say, to vex her I will execute in the clothes that

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: she so prais’d—to the court I’ll knock her back, foot her home again.

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: She hath despis’d me rejoicingly, and I’ll be merry in my revenge.
Enter Pisanio with the clothes.

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Be those the garments?

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: Ay, my noble lord.

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: How long is’t since she went to Milford Haven?

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: She can scarce be there yet.

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Bring this apparel to my chamber; that is the second thing that I have

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: commanded thee. The third is that thou wilt be a voluntary mute to my

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: design. Be but duteous and true, preferment shall tender itself to

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: thee. My revenge is now at Milford, would I had wings to follow it!

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Come, and be true.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: Thou bid’st me to my loss; for true to thee

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: Were to prove false, which I will never be,

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: To him that is most true. To Milford go,

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: And find not her whom thou pursuest. Flow, flow,

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: You heavenly blessings, on her! This fool’s speed

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: Be cross’d with slowness! Labour be his meed!
[_Exit._]

scenes.setting: Wales. Before the cave of Belarius.

lines.text: Enter Imogen alone, in boy’s clothes.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: I see a man’s life is a tedious one.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: I have tir’d myself, and for two nights together

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Have made the ground my bed. I should be sick

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: But that my resolution helps me. Milford,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: When from the mountain-top Pisanio show’d thee,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Thou wast within a ken. O Jove! I think

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Foundations fly the wretched; such, I mean,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Where they should be reliev’d. Two beggars told me

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: I could not miss my way. Will poor folks lie,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: That have afflictions on them, knowing ’tis

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: A punishment or trial? Yes; no wonder,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: When rich ones scarce tell true. To lapse in fulness

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Is sorer than to lie for need; and falsehood

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Is worse in kings than beggars. My dear lord!

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Thou art one o’ th’ false ones. Now I think on thee

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: My hunger’s gone; but even before, I was

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: At point to sink for food. But what is this?

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Here is a path to’t; ’tis some savage hold.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: I were best not call; I dare not call. Yet famine,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
