lines.text: Ere clean it o’erthrow nature, makes it valiant.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Plenty and peace breeds cowards; hardness ever

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Of hardiness is mother. Ho! who’s here?

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: If anything that’s civil, speak; if savage,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Take or lend. Ho! No answer? Then I’ll enter.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Best draw my sword; and if mine enemy

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: But fear the sword, like me, he’ll scarcely look on’t.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Such a foe, good heavens!
[_Exit into the cave._]
Enter Belarius, Guiderius and Arviragus.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: You, Polydore, have prov’d best woodman and

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Are master of the feast. Cadwal and I

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Will play the cook and servant; ’tis our match.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: The sweat of industry would dry and die

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: But for the end it works to. Come, our stomachs

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Will make what’s homely savoury; weariness

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Can snore upon the flint, when resty sloth

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Finds the down pillow hard. Now, peace be here,

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Poor house, that keep’st thyself!

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: I am thoroughly weary.

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: I am weak with toil, yet strong in appetite.

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: There is cold meat i’ th’ cave; we’ll browse on that

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Whilst what we have kill’d be cook’d.
[_Looking into the cave._]

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Stay, come not in.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: But that it eats our victuals, I should think

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Here were a fairy.

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: What’s the matter, sir?

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: By Jupiter, an angel! or, if not,

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: An earthly paragon! Behold divineness

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: No elder than a boy!
Enter Imogen.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Good masters, harm me not.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Before I enter’d here I call’d, and thought

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: To have begg’d or bought what I have took. Good troth,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: I have stol’n nought; nor would not though I had found

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Gold strew’d i’ th’ floor. Here’s money for my meat.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: I would have left it on the board, so soon

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: As I had made my meal, and parted

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: With pray’rs for the provider.

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Money, youth?

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: All gold and silver rather turn to dirt,

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: As ’tis no better reckon’d but of those

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: Who worship dirty gods.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: I see you’re angry.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Know, if you kill me for my fault, I should

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Have died had I not made it.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Whither bound?

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: To Milford Haven.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: What’s your name?

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Fidele, sir. I have a kinsman who

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Is bound for Italy; he embark’d at Milford;

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: To whom being going, almost spent with hunger,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: I am fall’n in this offence.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Prithee, fair youth,

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Think us no churls, nor measure our good minds

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: By this rude place we live in. Well encounter’d!

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: ’Tis almost night; you shall have better cheer

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Ere you depart, and thanks to stay and eat it.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Boys, bid him welcome.

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Were you a woman, youth,

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: I should woo hard but be your groom. In honesty

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: I bid for you as I’d buy.

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: I’ll make’t my comfort

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: He is a man. I’ll love him as my brother;

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: And such a welcome as I’d give to him

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: After long absence, such is yours. Most welcome!

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: Be sprightly, for you fall ’mongst friends.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: ’Mongst friends,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: If brothers. [_Aside._] Would it had been so that they

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Had been my father’s sons! Then had my prize

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Been less, and so more equal ballasting

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: To thee, Posthumus.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: He wrings at some distress.

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Would I could free’t!

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: Or I, whate’er it be,

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: What pain it cost, what danger! Gods!
[_Whispering._]

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Hark, boys.
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Great men,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: That had a court no bigger than this cave,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: That did attend themselves, and had the virtue

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Which their own conscience seal’d them, laying by

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: That nothing-gift of differing multitudes,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Could not out-peer these twain. Pardon me, gods!

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: I’d change my sex to be companion with them,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Since Leonatus false.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: It shall be so.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Boys, we’ll go dress our hunt. Fair youth, come in.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Discourse is heavy, fasting; when we have supp’d,

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: We’ll mannerly demand thee of thy story,

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: So far as thou wilt speak it.

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Pray draw near.

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: The night to th’ owl and morn to th’ lark less

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: welcome.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Thanks, sir.

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: I pray draw near.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter two Roman Senators and Tribunes.

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: This is the tenour of the Emperor’s writ:

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: That since the common men are now in action

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: ’Gainst the Pannonians and Dalmatians,

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: And that the legions now in Gallia are

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: Full weak to undertake our wars against

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: The fall’n-off Britons, that we do incite

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: The gentry to this business. He creates

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: Lucius proconsul; and to you, the tribunes,

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: For this immediate levy, he commands

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: His absolute commission. Long live Cæsar!

lines.speaker: TRIBUNE
lines.text: Is Lucius general of the forces?

lines.speaker: SECOND SENATOR
lines.text: Ay.

lines.speaker: TRIBUNE
lines.text: Remaining now in Gallia?

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: With those legions

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: Which I have spoke of, whereunto your levy

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: Must be supplyant. The words of your commission

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: Will tie you to the numbers and the time

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: Of their dispatch.

lines.speaker: TRIBUNE
lines.text: We will discharge our duty.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: Wales. Near the cave of Belarius.

lines.text: Enter Cloten alone.

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: I am near to th’ place where they should meet, if Pisanio have mapp’d

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: it truly. How fit his garments serve me! Why should his mistress, who

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: was made by him that made the tailor, not be fit too? The rather,

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: saving reverence of the word, for ’tis said a woman’s fitness comes by

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: fits. Therein I must play the workman. I dare speak it to myself, for

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: it is not vain-glory for a man and his glass to confer in his own

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: chamber; I mean, the lines of my body are as well drawn as his; no less

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: young, more strong, not beneath him in fortunes, beyond him in the

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: advantage of the time, above him in birth, alike conversant in general

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: services, and more remarkable in single oppositions. Yet this

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: imperceiverant thing loves him in my despite. What mortality is!

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Posthumus, thy head, which now is growing upon thy shoulders, shall

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: within this hour be off; thy mistress enforced; thy garments cut to

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: pieces before her face; and all this done, spurn her home to her

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: father, who may, haply, be a little angry for my so rough usage; but my

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: mother, having power of his testiness, shall turn all into my

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: commendations. My horse is tied up safe. Out, sword, and to a sore

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: purpose! Fortune, put them into my hand. This is the very description

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: of their meeting-place; and the fellow dares not deceive me.
[_Exit._]

scenes.setting: Wales. Before the cave of Belarius.

lines.text: Enter from the cave, Belarius, Guiderius, Arviragus and Imogen.
[_To Imogen._]

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: You are not well. Remain here in the cave;

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: We’ll come to you after hunting.
[_To Imogen._]

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: Brother, stay here.

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: Are we not brothers?

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: So man and man should be;

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: But clay and clay differs in dignity,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Whose dust is both alike. I am very sick.

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Go you to hunting; I’ll abide with him.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: So sick I am not, yet I am not well;

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: But not so citizen a wanton as

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: To seem to die ere sick. So please you, leave me;

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Stick to your journal course. The breach of custom

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Is breach of all. I am ill, but your being by me

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Cannot amend me; society is no comfort

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: To one not sociable. I am not very sick,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Since I can reason of it. Pray you trust me here.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: I’ll rob none but myself; and let me die,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Stealing so poorly.

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: I love thee; I have spoke it.

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: How much the quantity, the weight as much

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: As I do love my father.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: What? how? how?

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: If it be sin to say so, sir, I yoke me

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: In my good brother’s fault. I know not why

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: I love this youth, and I have heard you say

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: Love’s reason’s without reason. The bier at door,

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: And a demand who is’t shall die, I’d say

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: ‘My father, not this youth.’
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: O noble strain!

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: O worthiness of nature! breed of greatness!

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Cowards father cowards and base things sire base.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Nature hath meal and bran, contempt and grace.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: I’m not their father; yet who this should be

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Doth miracle itself, lov’d before me.—

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: ’Tis the ninth hour o’ th’ morn.

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: Brother, farewell.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: I wish ye sport.

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: Your health. [_To Belarius._] So please you, sir.
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: These are kind creatures. Gods, what lies I

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: have heard!

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Our courtiers say all’s savage but at court.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Experience, O, thou disprov’st report!

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Th’ imperious seas breed monsters; for the dish,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Poor tributary rivers as sweet fish.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: I am sick still; heart-sick. Pisanio,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: I’ll now taste of thy drug.
[_Swallows some._]

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: I could not stir him.

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: He said he was gentle, but unfortunate;

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Dishonestly afflicted, but yet honest.

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: Thus did he answer me; yet said hereafter

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: I might know more.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: To th’ field, to th’ field!

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: We’ll leave you for this time. Go in and rest.

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: We’ll not be long away.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Pray be not sick,

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: For you must be our huswife.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Well, or ill,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: I am bound to you.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: And shalt be ever.
[_Exit Imogen into the cave._]

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: This youth, howe’er distress’d, appears he hath had

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Good ancestors.

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: How angel-like he sings!

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: But his neat cookery! He cut our roots in characters,

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: And sauc’d our broths as Juno had been sick,

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: And he her dieter.

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: Nobly he yokes

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: A smiling with a sigh, as if the sigh

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: Was that it was for not being such a smile;

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: The smile mocking the sigh that it would fly

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: From so divine a temple to commix

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: With winds that sailors rail at.

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: I do note

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: That grief and patience, rooted in him both,

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Mingle their spurs together.

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: Grow patience!

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: And let the stinking elder, grief, untwine

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: His perishing root with the increasing vine!

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: It is great morning. Come, away! Who’s there?
Enter Cloten.

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: I cannot find those runagates; that villain

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Hath mock’d me. I am faint.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Those runagates?

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Means he not us? I partly know him; ’tis

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Cloten, the son o’ th’ Queen. I fear some ambush.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: I saw him not these many years, and yet

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: I know ’tis he. We are held as outlaws. Hence!

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: He is but one; you and my brother search

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: What companies are near. Pray you away;

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Let me alone with him.
[_Exeunt Belarius and Arviragus._]

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Soft! What are you

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: That fly me thus? Some villain mountaineers?

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: I have heard of such. What slave art thou?

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: A thing

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: More slavish did I ne’er than answering

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: A slave without a knock.

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Thou art a robber,

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: A law-breaker, a villain. Yield thee, thief.

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: To who? To thee? What art thou? Have not I

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: An arm as big as thine, a heart as big?

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Thy words, I grant, are bigger, for I wear not

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: My dagger in my mouth. Say what thou art;

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Why I should yield to thee.

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Thou villain base,

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Know’st me not by my clothes?

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: No, nor thy tailor, rascal,

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Who is thy grandfather; he made those clothes,

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Which, as it seems, make thee.

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Thou precious varlet,

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: My tailor made them not.

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Hence, then, and thank

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: The man that gave them thee. Thou art some fool;

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: I am loath to beat thee.

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Thou injurious thief,

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Hear but my name, and tremble.

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: What’s thy name?

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Cloten, thou villain.

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Cloten, thou double villain, be thy name,

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: I cannot tremble at it. Were it Toad, or Adder, Spider,

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: ’Twould move me sooner.

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: To thy further fear,

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Nay, to thy mere confusion, thou shalt know

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: I am son to th’ Queen.

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: I’m sorry for’t; not seeming

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: So worthy as thy birth.

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Art not afeard?

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Those that I reverence, those I fear—the wise;

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: At fools I laugh, not fear them.

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Die the death.

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: When I have slain thee with my proper hand,

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: I’ll follow those that even now fled hence,

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: And on the gates of Lud’s Town set your heads.

lines.speaker: CLOTEN
lines.text: Yield, rustic mountaineer.
[_Exeunt, fighting._]
Enter Belarius and Arviragus.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: No company’s abroad?

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: None in the world; you did mistake him, sure.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: I cannot tell; long is it since I saw him,

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: But time hath nothing blurr’d those lines of favour

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Which then he wore; the snatches in his voice,

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: And burst of speaking, were as his. I am absolute

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: ’Twas very Cloten.

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: In this place we left them.

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: I wish my brother make good time with him,

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: You say he is so fell.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Being scarce made up,

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: I mean to man, he had not apprehension

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Or roaring terrors; for defect of judgement

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Is oft the cease of fear.
Enter Guiderius with Cloten’s head.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: But, see, thy brother.

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: This Cloten was a fool, an empty purse;

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: There was no money in’t. Not Hercules

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Could have knock’d out his brains, for he had none;

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Yet I not doing this, the fool had borne

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: My head as I do his.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: What hast thou done?

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: I am perfect what: cut off one Cloten’s head,

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Son to the Queen, after his own report;

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Who call’d me traitor, mountaineer, and swore

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: With his own single hand he’d take us in,

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Displace our heads where, thank the gods, they grow,

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: And set them on Lud’s Town.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: We are all undone.

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Why, worthy father, what have we to lose

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: But that he swore to take, our lives? The law

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Protects not us; then why should we be tender

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: To let an arrogant piece of flesh threat us,

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Play judge and executioner all himself,

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: For we do fear the law? What company

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Discover you abroad?

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: No single soul

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Can we set eye on, but in all safe reason

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: He must have some attendants. Though his humour

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Was nothing but mutation, ay, and that

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: From one bad thing to worse, not frenzy, not

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Absolute madness could so far have rav’d,

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: To bring him here alone. Although perhaps

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: It may be heard at court that such as we

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Cave here, hunt here, are outlaws, and in time

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: May make some stronger head, the which he hearing,

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: As it is like him, might break out and swear

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: He’d fetch us in; yet is’t not probable

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: To come alone, either he so undertaking

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Or they so suffering. Then on good ground we fear,

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: If we do fear this body hath a tail

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: More perilous than the head.

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: Let ordinance

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: Come as the gods foresay it. Howsoe’er,

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: My brother hath done well.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: I had no mind

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: To hunt this day; the boy Fidele’s sickness

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Did make my way long forth.

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: With his own sword,

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Which he did wave against my throat, I have ta’en

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: His head from him. I’ll throw’t into the creek

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Behind our rock, and let it to the sea

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: And tell the fishes he’s the Queen’s son, Cloten.

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: That’s all I reck.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: I fear ’twill be reveng’d.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Would, Polydore, thou hadst not done’t! though valour

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Becomes thee well enough.

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: Would I had done’t,

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: So the revenge alone pursu’d me! Polydore,

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: I love thee brotherly, but envy much

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: Thou hast robb’d me of this deed. I would revenges,

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: That possible strength might meet, would seek us through,

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: And put us to our answer.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Well, ’tis done.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: We’ll hunt no more today, nor seek for danger

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Where there’s no profit. I prithee to our rock.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: You and Fidele play the cooks; I’ll stay

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Till hasty Polydore return, and bring him

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: To dinner presently.

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: Poor sick Fidele!

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: I’ll willingly to him; to gain his colour

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: I’d let a parish of such Cloten’s blood,

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: And praise myself for charity.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: O thou goddess,

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Thou divine Nature, thou thyself thou blazon’st

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: In these two princely boys! They are as gentle

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: As zephyrs blowing below the violet,

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Not wagging his sweet head; and yet as rough,

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Their royal blood enchaf’d, as the rud’st wind

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: That by the top doth take the mountain pine

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: And make him stoop to th’ vale. ’Tis wonder

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: That an invisible instinct should frame them

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: To royalty unlearn’d, honour untaught,

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Civility not seen from other, valour

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: That wildly grows in them, but yields a crop

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: As if it had been sow’d. Yet still it’s strange

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: What Cloten’s being here to us portends,

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Or what his death will bring us.
Enter Guiderius.

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Where’s my brother?

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: I have sent Cloten’s clotpoll down the stream,

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: In embassy to his mother; his body’s hostage

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: For his return.
[_Solemn music._]

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: My ingenious instrument!

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Hark, Polydore, it sounds. But what occasion

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Hath Cadwal now to give it motion? Hark!

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Is he at home?

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: He went hence even now.

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: What does he mean? Since death of my dear’st mother

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: It did not speak before. All solemn things

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Should answer solemn accidents. The matter?

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Triumphs for nothing and lamenting toys

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Is jollity for apes and grief for boys.

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Is Cadwal mad?
Enter Arviragus with Imogen as dead, bearing her in his arms.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Look, here he comes,

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: And brings the dire occasion in his arms

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Of what we blame him for!

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: The bird is dead

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: That we have made so much on. I had rather

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: Have skipp’d from sixteen years of age to sixty,

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: To have turn’d my leaping time into a crutch,

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: Than have seen this.

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: O sweetest, fairest lily!

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: My brother wears thee not the one half so well

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: As when thou grew’st thyself.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: O melancholy!

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Who ever yet could sound thy bottom? find

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: The ooze to show what coast thy sluggish crare

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Might’st easiliest harbour in? Thou blessed thing!

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Jove knows what man thou mightst have made; but I,

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Thou diedst, a most rare boy, of melancholy.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: How found you him?

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: Stark, as you see;

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: Thus smiling, as some fly had tickled slumber,

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: Not as death’s dart, being laugh’d at; his right cheek

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: Reposing on a cushion.

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Where?

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: O’ th’ floor;

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: His arms thus leagu’d. I thought he slept, and put

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: My clouted brogues from off my feet, whose rudeness

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: Answer’d my steps too loud.

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Why, he but sleeps.

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: If he be gone he’ll make his grave a bed;

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: With female fairies will his tomb be haunted,

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: And worms will not come to thee.

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: With fairest flowers,

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: Whilst summer lasts and I live here, Fidele,

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: I’ll sweeten thy sad grave. Thou shalt not lack

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: The flower that’s like thy face, pale primrose; nor

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: The azur’d hare-bell, like thy veins; no, nor

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: The leaf of eglantine, whom not to slander,

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: Out-sweet’ned not thy breath. The ruddock would,

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: With charitable bill (O bill, sore shaming

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: Those rich-left heirs that let their fathers lie

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: Without a monument!) bring thee all this;

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: Yea, and furr’d moss besides, when flow’rs are none,

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: To winter-ground thy corse—

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Prithee have done,

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: And do not play in wench-like words with that

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Which is so serious. Let us bury him,

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: And not protract with admiration what

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Is now due debt. To th’ grave.

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: Say, where shall’s lay him?

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: By good Euriphile, our mother.

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: Be’t so;

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: And let us, Polydore, though now our voices

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: Have got the mannish crack, sing him to th’ ground,

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: As once to our mother; use like note and words,

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: Save that Euriphile must be Fidele.

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Cadwal,

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: I cannot sing. I’ll weep, and word it with thee;

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: For notes of sorrow out of tune are worse

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Than priests and fanes that lie.

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: We’ll speak it, then.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Great griefs, I see, med’cine the less, for Cloten

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Is quite forgot. He was a queen’s son, boys;

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: And though he came our enemy, remember

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: He was paid for that. Though mean and mighty rotting

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Together have one dust, yet reverence,

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: That angel of the world, doth make distinction

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Of place ’tween high and low. Our foe was princely;

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: And though you took his life, as being our foe,

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Yet bury him as a prince.

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Pray you fetch him hither.

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Thersites’ body is as good as Ajax’,

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: When neither are alive.

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: If you’ll go fetch him,

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: We’ll say our song the whilst. Brother, begin.
[_Exit Belarius._]

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Nay, Cadwal, we must lay his head to th’ East;

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: My father hath a reason for’t.

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: ’Tis true.

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Come on, then, and remove him.

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: So. Begin.

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: SONG

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: _    Fear no more the heat o’ th’ sun,

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Nor the furious winter’s rages;

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Thou thy worldly task hast done,

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Home art gone, and ta’en thy wages.

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Golden lads and girls all must,

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: As chimney-sweepers, come to dust._

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: _    Fear no more the frown o’ th’ great;

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: Thou art past the tyrant’s stroke.

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: Care no more to clothe and eat;

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: To thee the reed is as the oak.

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: The sceptre, learning, physic, must

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: All follow this and come to dust._

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: _    Fear no more the lightning flash._

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: _        Nor th’ all-dreaded thunder-stone._

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: _    Fear not slander, censure rash;_

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: _    Thou hast finish’d joy and moan._

lines.speaker: BOTH
lines.text: _    All lovers young, all lovers must

lines.speaker: BOTH
lines.text: Consign to thee and come to dust._

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: _    No exorciser harm thee!_

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: _    Nor no witchcraft charm thee!_

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: _    Ghost unlaid forbear thee!_

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: _    Nothing ill come near thee!_

lines.speaker: BOTH
lines.text: _    Quiet consummation have,

lines.speaker: BOTH
lines.text: And renowned be thy grave!_
Enter Belarius with the body of Cloten.

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: We have done our obsequies. Come, lay him down.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Here’s a few flowers; but ’bout midnight, more.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: The herbs that have on them cold dew o’ th’ night

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Are strewings fit’st for graves. Upon their faces.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: You were as flow’rs, now wither’d. Even so

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: These herblets shall which we upon you strew.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Come on, away. Apart upon our knees.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: The ground that gave them first has them again.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Their pleasures here are past, so is their pain.
[_Exeunt all but Imogen._]
[_Awaking._]

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Yes, sir, to Milford Haven. Which is the way?

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: I thank you. By yond bush? Pray, how far thither?

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: ’Ods pittikins! can it be six mile yet?

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: I have gone all night. Faith, I’ll lie down and sleep.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: But, soft! no bedfellow. O gods and goddesses!
[_Seeing the body._]

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: These flow’rs are like the pleasures of the world;

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: This bloody man, the care on’t. I hope I dream;

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: For so I thought I was a cave-keeper,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: And cook to honest creatures. But ’tis not so;

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: ’Twas but a bolt of nothing, shot at nothing,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Which the brain makes of fumes. Our very eyes

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Are sometimes, like our judgements, blind. Good faith,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: I tremble still with fear; but if there be

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Yet left in heaven as small a drop of pity

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: As a wren’s eye, fear’d gods, a part of it!

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: The dream’s here still. Even when I wake it is

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Without me, as within me; not imagin’d, felt.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: A headless man? The garments of Posthumus?

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: I know the shape of’s leg; this is his hand,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: His foot Mercurial, his Martial thigh,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: The brawns of Hercules; but his Jovial face—

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Murder in heaven! How! ’Tis gone. Pisanio,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: All curses madded Hecuba gave the Greeks,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: And mine to boot, be darted on thee! Thou,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Conspir’d with that irregulous devil, Cloten,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Hath here cut off my lord. To write and read

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Be henceforth treacherous! Damn’d Pisanio

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Hath with his forged letters (damn’d Pisanio)

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: From this most bravest vessel of the world

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Struck the main-top. O Posthumus! alas,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Where is thy head? Where’s that? Ay me! where’s that?

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Pisanio might have kill’d thee at the heart,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: And left this head on. How should this be? Pisanio?

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: ’Tis he and Cloten; malice and lucre in them

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Have laid this woe here. O, ’tis pregnant, pregnant!

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: The drug he gave me, which he said was precious

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: And cordial to me, have I not found it

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Murd’rous to th’ senses? That confirms it home.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: This is Pisanio’s deed, and Cloten. O!

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Give colour to my pale cheek with thy blood,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: That we the horrider may seem to those

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Which chance to find us. O, my lord, my lord!
[_Falls fainting on the body._]
Enter Lucius, Captains and a Soothsayer.

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: To them the legions garrison’d in Gallia,

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: After your will, have cross’d the sea, attending

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: You here at Milford Haven; with your ships,

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: They are in readiness.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: But what from Rome?

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: The Senate hath stirr’d up the confiners

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: And gentlemen of Italy, most willing spirits,

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: That promise noble service; and they come

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: Under the conduct of bold Iachimo,

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: Sienna’s brother.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: When expect you them?

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: With the next benefit o’ th’ wind.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: This forwardness

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Makes our hopes fair. Command our present numbers

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Be muster’d; bid the captains look to’t. Now, sir,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: What have you dream’d of late of this war’s purpose?

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: Last night the very gods show’d me a vision

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: (I fast and pray’d for their intelligence) thus:

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: I saw Jove’s bird, the Roman eagle, wing’d

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: From the spongy south to this part of the west,

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: There vanish’d in the sunbeams; which portends,

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: Unless my sins abuse my divination,

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: Success to th’ Roman host.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Dream often so,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: And never false. Soft, ho! what trunk is here

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Without his top? The ruin speaks that sometime

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: It was a worthy building. How? a page?

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Or dead or sleeping on him? But dead, rather;

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: For nature doth abhor to make his bed

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: With the defunct, or sleep upon the dead.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Let’s see the boy’s face.

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: He’s alive, my lord.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: He’ll then instruct us of this body. Young one,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Inform us of thy fortunes; for it seems

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: They crave to be demanded. Who is this

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Thou mak’st thy bloody pillow? Or who was he

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: That, otherwise than noble nature did,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Hath alter’d that good picture? What’s thy interest

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: In this sad wreck? How came’t? Who is’t?

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: What art thou?

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: I am nothing; or if not,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Nothing to be were better. This was my master,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: A very valiant Briton and a good,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: That here by mountaineers lies slain. Alas!

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: There is no more such masters. I may wander

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: From east to occident; cry out for service;

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Try many, all good; serve truly; never

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Find such another master.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: ’Lack, good youth!

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Thou mov’st no less with thy complaining than

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Thy master in bleeding. Say his name, good friend.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Richard du Champ. [_Aside._] If I do lie, and do

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: No harm by it, though the gods hear, I hope

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: They’ll pardon it.—Say you, sir?

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Thy name?

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Fidele, sir.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Thou dost approve thyself the very same;

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Thy name well fits thy faith, thy faith thy name.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Wilt take thy chance with me? I will not say

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Thou shalt be so well master’d; but, be sure,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: No less belov’d. The Roman Emperor’s letters,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Sent by a consul to me, should not sooner

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Than thine own worth prefer thee. Go with me.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: I’ll follow, sir. But first, an’t please the gods,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: I’ll hide my master from the flies, as deep

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: As these poor pickaxes can dig; and when

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: With wild wood-leaves and weeds I ha’ strew’d his grave,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: And on it said a century of prayers,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Such as I can, twice o’er, I’ll weep and sigh;

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: And leaving so his service, follow you,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: So please you entertain me.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Ay, good youth;

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: And rather father thee than master thee.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: My friends,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: The boy hath taught us manly duties; let us

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Find out the prettiest daisied plot we can,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: And make him with our pikes and partisans

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: A grave. Come, arm him. Boy, he is preferr’d

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: By thee to us; and he shall be interr’d

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: As soldiers can. Be cheerful; wipe thine eyes.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Some falls are means the happier to arise.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Cymbeline, Lords, Pisanio and Attendants.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Again! and bring me word how ’tis with her.
[_Exit an Attendant._]

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: A fever with the absence of her son;

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: A madness, of which her life’s in danger. Heavens,

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: How deeply you at once do touch me! Imogen,

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: The great part of my comfort, gone; my queen

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Upon a desperate bed, and in a time

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: When fearful wars point at me; her son gone,

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: So needful for this present. It strikes me past

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: The hope of comfort. But for thee, fellow,

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Who needs must know of her departure and

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Dost seem so ignorant, we’ll enforce it from thee

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: By a sharp torture.

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: Sir, my life is yours;

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: I humbly set it at your will; but for my mistress,

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: I nothing know where she remains, why gone,

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: Nor when she purposes return. Beseech your Highness,

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: Hold me your loyal servant.

lines.speaker: LORD
lines.text: Good my liege,

lines.speaker: LORD
lines.text: The day that she was missing he was here.

lines.speaker: LORD
lines.text: I dare be bound he’s true and shall perform

lines.speaker: LORD
lines.text: All parts of his subjection loyally. For Cloten,

lines.speaker: LORD
lines.text: There wants no diligence in seeking him,

lines.speaker: LORD
lines.text: And will no doubt be found.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: The time is troublesome.
[_To Pisanio._]

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: We’ll slip you for a season; but our jealousy

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Does yet depend.

lines.speaker: LORD
lines.text: So please your Majesty,

lines.speaker: LORD
lines.text: The Roman legions, all from Gallia drawn,

lines.speaker: LORD
lines.text: Are landed on your coast, with a supply

lines.speaker: LORD
lines.text: Of Roman gentlemen by the Senate sent.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Now for the counsel of my son and queen!

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: I am amaz’d with matter.

lines.speaker: LORD
lines.text: Good my liege,

lines.speaker: LORD
lines.text: Your preparation can affront no less

lines.speaker: LORD
lines.text: Than what you hear of. Come more, for more you’re ready.

lines.speaker: LORD
lines.text: The want is but to put those pow’rs in motion

lines.speaker: LORD
lines.text: That long to move.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: I thank you. Let’s withdraw,

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: And meet the time as it seeks us. We fear not

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: What can from Italy annoy us; but

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: We grieve at chances here. Away!
[_Exeunt all but Pisanio._]

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: I heard no letter from my master since

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: I wrote him Imogen was slain. ’Tis strange.

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: Nor hear I from my mistress, who did promise

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: To yield me often tidings. Neither know I

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: What is betid to Cloten, but remain

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: Perplex’d in all. The heavens still must work.

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: Wherein I am false I am honest; not true, to be true.

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: These present wars shall find I love my country,

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: Even to the note o’ th’ King, or I’ll fall in them.

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: All other doubts, by time let them be clear’d:

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: Fortune brings in some boats that are not steer’d.
[_Exit._]

scenes.setting: Wales. Before the cave of Belarius.

lines.text: Enter Belarius, Guiderius and Arviragus.

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: The noise is round about us.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Let us from it.

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: What pleasure, sir, find we in life, to lock it

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: From action and adventure?

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Nay, what hope

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Have we in hiding us? This way the Romans

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Must or for Britons slay us, or receive us

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: For barbarous and unnatural revolts

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: During their use, and slay us after.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Sons,

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: We’ll higher to the mountains; there secure us.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: To the King’s party there’s no going. Newness

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Of Cloten’s death (we being not known, not muster’d

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Among the bands) may drive us to a render

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Where we have liv’d, and so extort from’s that

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Which we have done, whose answer would be death,

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Drawn on with torture.

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: This is, sir, a doubt

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: In such a time nothing becoming you

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Nor satisfying us.

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: It is not likely

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: That when they hear the Roman horses neigh,

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: Behold their quarter’d fires, have both their eyes

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: And ears so cloy’d importantly as now,

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: That they will waste their time upon our note,

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: To know from whence we are.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: O, I am known

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Of many in the army. Many years,

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Though Cloten then but young, you see, not wore him

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: From my remembrance. And, besides, the King

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Hath not deserv’d my service nor your loves,

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Who find in my exile the want of breeding,

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: The certainty of this hard life; aye hopeless

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: To have the courtesy your cradle promis’d,

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: But to be still hot summer’s tanlings and

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: The shrinking slaves of winter.

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Than be so,

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Better to cease to be. Pray, sir, to th’ army.

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: I and my brother are not known; yourself

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: So out of thought, and thereto so o’ergrown,

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: Cannot be questioned.

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: By this sun that shines,

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: I’ll thither. What thing is’t that I never

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: Did see man die! scarce ever look’d on blood

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: But that of coward hares, hot goats, and venison!

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: Never bestrid a horse, save one that had

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: A rider like myself, who ne’er wore rowel

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: Nor iron on his heel! I am asham’d

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: To look upon the holy sun, to have

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: The benefit of his blest beams, remaining

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: So long a poor unknown.

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: By heavens, I’ll go!

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: If you will bless me, sir, and give me leave,

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: I’ll take the better care; but if you will not,

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: The hazard therefore due fall on me by

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: The hands of Romans!

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: So say I. Amen.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: No reason I, since of your lives you set

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: So slight a valuation, should reserve

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: My crack’d one to more care. Have with you, boys!

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: If in your country wars you chance to die,

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: That is my bed too, lads, and there I’ll lie.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Lead, lead. [_Aside._] The time seems long; their blood thinks scorn

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Till it fly out and show them princes born.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Posthumus alone, with a bloody handkerchief.

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Yea, bloody cloth, I’ll keep thee; for I wish’d

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Thou shouldst be colour’d thus. You married ones,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: If each of you should take this course, how many

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Must murder wives much better than themselves

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: For wrying but a little! O Pisanio!

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Every good servant does not all commands;

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: No bond but to do just ones. Gods! if you

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Should have ta’en vengeance on my faults, I never

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Had liv’d to put on this; so had you saved

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: The noble Imogen to repent, and struck

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Me, wretch more worth your vengeance. But alack,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: You snatch some hence for little faults; that’s love,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: To have them fall no more. You some permit

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: To second ills with ills, each elder worse,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: And make them dread it, to the doers’ thrift.

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: But Imogen is your own. Do your best wills,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: And make me blest to obey. I am brought hither

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Among th’ Italian gentry, and to fight

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Against my lady’s kingdom. ’Tis enough

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: That, Britain, I have kill’d thy mistress; peace!

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: I’ll give no wound to thee. Therefore, good heavens,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Hear patiently my purpose. I’ll disrobe me

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Of these Italian weeds, and suit myself

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: As does a Britain peasant. So I’ll fight

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Against the part I come with; so I’ll die

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: For thee, O Imogen, even for whom my life

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Is every breath a death. And thus unknown,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Pitied nor hated, to the face of peril

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Myself I’ll dedicate. Let me make men know

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: More valour in me than my habits show.

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Gods, put the strength o’ th’ Leonati in me!

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: To shame the guise o’ th’ world, I will begin

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: The fashion less without and more within.
[_Exit._]

scenes.setting: Britain. A field of battle between the British and Roman

lines.text: camps.

Enter Lucius, Iachimo and the Roman army at one door, and the British army at another, Leonatus Posthumus following like a poor soldier. They march over and go out. Alarums. Then enter again, in skirmish, Iachimo and Posthumus. He vanquisheth and disarmeth Iachimo and then leaves him.

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: The heaviness and guilt within my bosom

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Takes off my manhood. I have belied a lady,

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: The Princess of this country, and the air on’t

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Revengingly enfeebles me; or could this carl,

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: A very drudge of nature’s, have subdu’d me

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: In my profession? Knighthoods and honours borne

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: As I wear mine are titles but of scorn.

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: If that thy gentry, Britain, go before

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: This lout as he exceeds our lords, the odds

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Is that we scarce are men, and you are gods.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: The battle continues; the Britons fly; Cymbeline is taken. Then enter

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: to his rescue Belarius, Guiderius and Arviragus.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Stand, stand! We have th’ advantage of the ground;

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: The lane is guarded; nothing routs us but

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: The villainy of our fears.

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS and ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: Stand, stand, and fight!
Enter Posthumus and seconds the Britons; they rescue Cymbeline and exeunt. Then re-enter Lucius and Iachimo with Imogen.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Away, boy, from the troops, and save thyself;

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: For friends kill friends, and the disorder’s such

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: As war were hoodwink’d.

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: ’Tis their fresh supplies.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: It is a day turn’d strangely. Or betimes

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Let’s reinforce or fly.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Posthumus and a Briton Lord.

lines.speaker: LORD
lines.text: Cam’st thou from where they made the stand?

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: I did:

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Though you, it seems, come from the fliers.

lines.speaker: LORD
lines.text: I did.

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: No blame be to you, sir, for all was lost,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: But that the heavens fought. The King himself

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Of his wings destitute, the army broken,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: And but the backs of Britons seen, all flying,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Through a strait lane; the enemy, full-hearted,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Lolling the tongue with slaught’ring, having work

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: More plentiful than tools to do’t, struck down

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Some mortally, some slightly touch’d, some falling

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Merely through fear, that the strait pass was damm’d

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: With dead men hurt behind, and cowards living

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: To die with length’ned shame.

lines.speaker: LORD
lines.text: Where was this lane?

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Close by the battle, ditch’d, and wall’d with turf,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Which gave advantage to an ancient soldier,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: An honest one, I warrant, who deserv’d

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: So long a breeding as his white beard came to,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: In doing this for’s country. Athwart the lane

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: He, with two striplings (lads more like to run

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: The country base than to commit such slaughter;

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: With faces fit for masks, or rather fairer

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Than those for preservation cas’d or shame)

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Made good the passage, cried to those that fled

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: ‘Our Britain’s harts die flying, not our men.

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: To darkness fleet souls that fly backwards! Stand;

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Or we are Romans and will give you that,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Like beasts, which you shun beastly, and may save

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: But to look back in frown. Stand, stand!’ These three,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Three thousand confident, in act as many—

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: For three performers are the file when all

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: The rest do nothing—with this word ‘Stand, stand!’

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Accommodated by the place, more charming

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: With their own nobleness, which could have turn’d

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: A distaff to a lance, gilded pale looks,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Part shame, part spirit renew’d; that some turn’d coward

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: But by example (O, a sin in war

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Damn’d in the first beginners) ’gan to look

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: The way that they did and to grin like lions

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Upon the pikes o’ th’ hunters. Then began

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: A stop i’ th’ chaser, a retire; anon

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: A rout, confusion thick. Forthwith they fly,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Chickens, the way which they stoop’d eagles; slaves,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: The strides they victors made; and now our cowards,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Like fragments in hard voyages, became

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: The life o’ th’ need. Having found the back-door open

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Of the unguarded hearts, heavens, how they wound!

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Some slain before, some dying, some their friends

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: O’erborne i’ th’ former wave. Ten chas’d by one

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Are now each one the slaughterman of twenty.

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Those that would die or ere resist are grown

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: The mortal bugs o’ th’ field.

lines.speaker: LORD
lines.text: This was strange chance:

lines.speaker: LORD
lines.text: A narrow lane, an old man, and two boys.

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Nay, do not wonder at it; you are made

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Rather to wonder at the things you hear

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Than to work any. Will you rhyme upon’t,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: And vent it for a mock’ry? Here is one:

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: ‘Two boys, an old man (twice a boy), a lane,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Preserv’d the Britons, was the Romans’ bane.’

lines.speaker: LORD
lines.text: Nay, be not angry, sir.

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: ’Lack, to what end?

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Who dares not stand his foe I’ll be his friend;

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: For if he’ll do as he is made to do,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: I know he’ll quickly fly my friendship too.

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: You have put me into rhyme.

lines.speaker: LORD
lines.text: Farewell; you’re angry.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Still going? This is a lord! O noble misery,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: To be i’ th’ field and ask ‘What news?’ of me!

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Today how many would have given their honours

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: To have sav’d their carcasses! took heel to do’t,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: And yet died too! I, in mine own woe charm’d,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Could not find death where I did hear him groan,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Nor feel him where he struck. Being an ugly monster,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: ’Tis strange he hides him in fresh cups, soft beds,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Sweet words; or hath moe ministers than we

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: That draw his knives i’ th’ war. Well, I will find him;

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: For being now a favourer to the Briton,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: No more a Briton, I have resum’d again

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: The part I came in. Fight I will no more,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: But yield me to the veriest hind that shall

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Once touch my shoulder. Great the slaughter is

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Here made by th’ Roman; great the answer be

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Britons must take. For me, my ransom’s death;

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: On either side I come to spend my breath,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Which neither here I’ll keep nor bear again,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: But end it by some means for Imogen.
Enter two British Captains and soldiers.

lines.speaker: FIRST CAPTAIN
lines.text: Great Jupiter be prais’d! Lucius is taken.

lines.speaker: FIRST CAPTAIN
lines.text: ’Tis thought the old man and his sons were angels.

lines.speaker: SECOND CAPTAIN
lines.text: There was a fourth man, in a silly habit,

lines.speaker: SECOND CAPTAIN
lines.text: That gave th’ affront with them.

lines.speaker: FIRST CAPTAIN
lines.text: So ’tis reported;

lines.speaker: FIRST CAPTAIN
lines.text: But none of ’em can be found. Stand! who’s there?

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: A Roman,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Who had not now been drooping here if seconds

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Had answer’d him.

lines.speaker: SECOND CAPTAIN
lines.text: Lay hands on him; a dog!

lines.speaker: SECOND CAPTAIN
lines.text: A leg of Rome shall not return to tell

lines.speaker: SECOND CAPTAIN
lines.text: What crows have peck’d them here. He brags his service,

lines.speaker: SECOND CAPTAIN
lines.text: As if he were of note. Bring him to th’ King.
Enter Cymbeline, Belarius, Guiderius, Arviragus, Pisanio and Roman captives. The Captains present Posthumus to Cymbeline, who delivers him over to a gaoler.
[_Exeunt omnes._]
Enter Posthumus and two Gaolers.

lines.speaker: FIRST GAOLER
lines.text: You shall not now be stol’n, you have locks upon you;

lines.speaker: FIRST GAOLER
lines.text: So graze as you find pasture.

lines.speaker: SECOND GAOLER
lines.text: Ay, or a stomach.
[_Exeunt Gaolers._]

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Most welcome, bondage! for thou art a way,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: I think, to liberty. Yet am I better

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Than one that’s sick o’ th’ gout, since he had rather

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Groan so in perpetuity than be cur’d

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: By th’ sure physician death, who is the key

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: T’ unbar these locks. My conscience, thou art fetter’d

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: More than my shanks and wrists; you good gods, give me

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: The penitent instrument to pick that bolt,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Then, free for ever! Is’t enough I am sorry?

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: So children temporal fathers do appease;

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Gods are more full of mercy. Must I repent,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: I cannot do it better than in gyves,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Desir’d more than constrain’d. To satisfy,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: If of my freedom ’tis the main part, take

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: No stricter render of me than my all.

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: I know you are more clement than vile men,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Who of their broken debtors take a third,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: A sixth, a tenth, letting them thrive again

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: On their abatement; that’s not my desire.

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: For Imogen’s dear life take mine; and though

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: ’Tis not so dear, yet ’tis a life; you coin’d it.

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: ’Tween man and man they weigh not every stamp;

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Though light, take pieces for the figure’s sake;

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: You rather mine, being yours. And so, great pow’rs,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: If you will take this audit, take this life,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: And cancel these cold bonds. O Imogen!

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: I’ll speak to thee in silence.
[_Sleeps._]

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Solemn music. Enter, as in an apparition, Sicilius Leonatus, father to

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Posthumus, an old man attired like a warrior; leading in his hand an

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: ancient matron, his wife and Mother to Posthumus, with music before

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: them. Then, after other music, follows the two young Leonati, brothers

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: to Posthumus, with wounds, as they died in the wars. They circle

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Posthumus round as he lies sleeping.

lines.speaker: SICILIUS
lines.text: No more, thou thunder-master, show

lines.speaker: SICILIUS
lines.text: Thy spite on mortal flies.

lines.speaker: SICILIUS
lines.text: With Mars fall out, with Juno chide,

lines.speaker: SICILIUS
lines.text: That thy adulteries

lines.speaker: SICILIUS
lines.text: Rates and revenges.

lines.speaker: SICILIUS
lines.text: Hath my poor boy done aught but well,

lines.speaker: SICILIUS
lines.text: Whose face I never saw?

lines.speaker: SICILIUS
lines.text: I died whilst in the womb he stay’d

lines.speaker: SICILIUS
lines.text: Attending nature’s law;

lines.speaker: SICILIUS
lines.text: Whose father then, as men report

lines.speaker: SICILIUS
lines.text: Thou orphans’ father art,

lines.speaker: SICILIUS
lines.text: Thou shouldst have been, and shielded him

lines.speaker: SICILIUS
lines.text: From this earth-vexing smart.

lines.speaker: MOTHER
lines.text: Lucina lent not me her aid,

lines.speaker: MOTHER
lines.text: But took me in my throes,

lines.speaker: MOTHER
lines.text: That from me was Posthumus ripp’d,

lines.speaker: MOTHER
lines.text: Came crying ’mongst his foes,

lines.speaker: MOTHER
lines.text: A thing of pity.

lines.speaker: SICILIUS
lines.text: Great Nature like his ancestry

lines.speaker: SICILIUS
lines.text: Moulded the stuff so fair

lines.speaker: SICILIUS
lines.text: That he deserv’d the praise o’ th’ world

lines.speaker: SICILIUS
lines.text: As great Sicilius’ heir.

lines.speaker: FIRST BROTHER
lines.text: When once he was mature for man,

lines.speaker: FIRST BROTHER
lines.text: In Britain where was he

lines.speaker: FIRST BROTHER
lines.text: That could stand up his parallel,

lines.speaker: FIRST BROTHER
lines.text: Or fruitful object be

lines.speaker: FIRST BROTHER
lines.text: In eye of Imogen, that best

lines.speaker: FIRST BROTHER
lines.text: Could deem his dignity?

lines.speaker: MOTHER
lines.text: With marriage wherefore was he mock’d,

lines.speaker: MOTHER
lines.text: To be exil’d and thrown

lines.speaker: MOTHER
lines.text: From Leonati seat and cast

lines.speaker: MOTHER
lines.text: From her his dearest one,

lines.speaker: MOTHER
lines.text: Sweet Imogen?

lines.speaker: SICILIUS
lines.text: Why did you suffer Iachimo,

lines.speaker: SICILIUS
lines.text: Slight thing of Italy,

lines.speaker: SICILIUS
lines.text: To taint his nobler heart and brain

lines.speaker: SICILIUS
lines.text: With needless jealousy,

lines.speaker: SICILIUS
lines.text: And to become the geck and scorn

lines.speaker: SICILIUS
lines.text: O’ th’ other’s villainy?

lines.speaker: SECOND BROTHER
lines.text: For this from stiller seats we came,

lines.speaker: SECOND BROTHER
lines.text: Our parents and us twain,

lines.speaker: SECOND BROTHER
lines.text: That, striking in our country’s cause,

lines.speaker: SECOND BROTHER
lines.text: Fell bravely and were slain,

lines.speaker: SECOND BROTHER
lines.text: Our fealty and Tenantius’ right

lines.speaker: SECOND BROTHER
lines.text: With honour to maintain.

lines.speaker: FIRST BROTHER
lines.text: Like hardiment Posthumus hath

lines.speaker: FIRST BROTHER
lines.text: To Cymbeline perform’d.

lines.speaker: FIRST BROTHER
lines.text: Then, Jupiter, thou king of gods,

lines.speaker: FIRST BROTHER
lines.text: Why hast thou thus adjourn’d

lines.speaker: FIRST BROTHER
lines.text: The graces for his merits due,

lines.speaker: FIRST BROTHER
lines.text: Being all to dolours turn’d?

lines.speaker: SICILIUS
lines.text: Thy crystal window ope; look out;

lines.speaker: SICILIUS
lines.text: No longer exercise

lines.speaker: SICILIUS
lines.text: Upon a valiant race thy harsh

lines.speaker: SICILIUS
lines.text: And potent injuries.

lines.speaker: MOTHER
lines.text: Since, Jupiter, our son is good,

lines.speaker: MOTHER
lines.text: Take off his miseries.

lines.speaker: SICILIUS
lines.text: Peep through thy marble mansion. Help!

lines.speaker: SICILIUS
lines.text: Or we poor ghosts will cry

lines.speaker: SICILIUS
lines.text: To th’ shining synod of the rest

lines.speaker: SICILIUS
lines.text: Against thy deity.

lines.speaker: BROTHERS
lines.text: Help, Jupiter! or we appeal,

lines.speaker: BROTHERS
lines.text: And from thy justice fly.

lines.speaker: BROTHERS
lines.text: Jupiter descends in thunder and lightning, sitting upon an eagle. He

lines.speaker: BROTHERS
lines.text: throws a thunderbolt. The Ghosts fall on their knees.

lines.speaker: JUPITER
lines.text: No more, you petty spirits of region low,

lines.speaker: JUPITER
lines.text: Offend our hearing; hush! How dare you ghosts

lines.speaker: JUPITER
lines.text: Accuse the Thunderer whose bolt, you know,

lines.speaker: JUPITER
lines.text: Sky-planted, batters all rebelling coasts?

lines.speaker: JUPITER
lines.text: Poor shadows of Elysium, hence and rest

lines.speaker: JUPITER
lines.text: Upon your never-withering banks of flow’rs.

lines.speaker: JUPITER
lines.text: Be not with mortal accidents opprest:

lines.speaker: JUPITER
lines.text: No care of yours it is; you know ’tis ours.

lines.speaker: JUPITER
lines.text: Whom best I love I cross; to make my gift,

lines.speaker: JUPITER
lines.text: The more delay’d, delighted. Be content;

lines.speaker: JUPITER
lines.text: Your low-laid son our godhead will uplift;

lines.speaker: JUPITER
lines.text: His comforts thrive, his trials well are spent.

lines.speaker: JUPITER
lines.text: Our Jovial star reign’d at his birth, and in

lines.speaker: JUPITER
lines.text: Our temple was he married. Rise and fade!

lines.speaker: JUPITER
lines.text: He shall be lord of Lady Imogen,

lines.speaker: JUPITER
lines.text: And happier much by his affliction made.

lines.speaker: JUPITER
lines.text: This tablet lay upon his breast, wherein

lines.speaker: JUPITER
lines.text: Our pleasure his full fortune doth confine;

lines.speaker: JUPITER
lines.text: And so, away; no farther with your din

lines.speaker: JUPITER
lines.text: Express impatience, lest you stir up mine.

lines.speaker: JUPITER
lines.text: Mount, eagle, to my palace crystalline.
[_Ascends._]

lines.speaker: SICILIUS
lines.text: He came in thunder; his celestial breath

lines.speaker: SICILIUS
lines.text: Was sulphurous to smell; the holy eagle

lines.speaker: SICILIUS
lines.text: Stoop’d as to foot us. His ascension is

lines.speaker: SICILIUS
lines.text: More sweet than our blest fields. His royal bird

lines.speaker: SICILIUS
lines.text: Prunes the immortal wing, and cloys his beak,

lines.speaker: SICILIUS
lines.text: As when his god is pleas’d.

lines.speaker: ALL
lines.text: Thanks, Jupiter!

lines.speaker: SICILIUS
lines.text: The marble pavement closes, he is enter’d

lines.speaker: SICILIUS
lines.text: His radiant roof. Away! and, to be blest,

lines.speaker: SICILIUS
lines.text: Let us with care perform his great behest.
[_Ghosts vanish._]
[_Waking._]

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Sleep, thou has been a grandsire and begot

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: A father to me; and thou hast created

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: A mother and two brothers. But, O scorn,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Gone! They went hence so soon as they were born.

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: And so I am awake. Poor wretches, that depend

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: On greatness’ favour, dream as I have done;

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Wake and find nothing. But, alas, I swerve;

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Many dream not to find, neither deserve,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: And yet are steep’d in favours; so am I,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: That have this golden chance, and know not why.

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: What fairies haunt this ground? A book? O rare one!

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Be not, as is our fangled world, a garment

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Nobler than that it covers. Let thy effects

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: So follow to be most unlike our courtiers,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: As good as promise.
[_Reads._]

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
