lines.text: _When as a lion’s whelp shall, to himself unknown, without

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: seeking find, and be embrac’d by a piece of tender air; and when from a

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: stately cedar shall be lopp’d branches which, being dead many years,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: shall after revive, be jointed to the old stock, and freshly grow; then

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: shall Posthumus end his miseries, Britain be fortunate and flourish in

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: peace and plenty._

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: ’Tis still a dream, or else such stuff as madmen

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Tongue, and brain not; either both or nothing,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Or senseless speaking, or a speaking such

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: As sense cannot untie. Be what it is,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: The action of my life is like it, which

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: I’ll keep, if but for sympathy.
Enter Gaoler.

lines.speaker: GAOLER
lines.text: Come, sir, are you ready for death?

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Over-roasted rather; ready long ago.

lines.speaker: GAOLER
lines.text: Hanging is the word, sir; if you be ready for that, you are well

lines.speaker: GAOLER
lines.text: cook’d.

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: So, if I prove a good repast to the spectators, the dish pays the shot.

lines.speaker: GAOLER
lines.text: A heavy reckoning for you, sir. But the comfort is, you shall be called

lines.speaker: GAOLER
lines.text: to no more payments, fear no more tavern bills, which are often the

lines.speaker: GAOLER
lines.text: sadness of parting, as the procuring of mirth. You come in faint for

lines.speaker: GAOLER
lines.text: want of meat, depart reeling with too much drink; sorry that you have

lines.speaker: GAOLER
lines.text: paid too much, and sorry that you are paid too much; purse and brain

lines.speaker: GAOLER
lines.text: both empty; the brain the heavier for being too light, the purse too

lines.speaker: GAOLER
lines.text: light, being drawn of heaviness. O, of this contradiction you shall now

lines.speaker: GAOLER
lines.text: be quit. O, the charity of a penny cord! It sums up thousands in a

lines.speaker: GAOLER
lines.text: trice. You have no true debitor and creditor but it; of what’s past,

lines.speaker: GAOLER
lines.text: is, and to come, the discharge. Your neck, sir, is pen, book, and

lines.speaker: GAOLER
lines.text: counters; so the acquittance follows.

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: I am merrier to die than thou art to live.

lines.speaker: GAOLER
lines.text: Indeed, sir, he that sleeps feels not the toothache. But a man that

lines.speaker: GAOLER
lines.text: were to sleep your sleep, and a hangman to help him to bed, I think he

lines.speaker: GAOLER
lines.text: would change places with his officer; for look you, sir, you know not

lines.speaker: GAOLER
lines.text: which way you shall go.

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Yes indeed do I, fellow.

lines.speaker: GAOLER
lines.text: Your death has eyes in’s head, then; I have not seen him so pictur’d.

lines.speaker: GAOLER
lines.text: You must either be directed by some that take upon them to know, or to

lines.speaker: GAOLER
lines.text: take upon yourself that which I am sure you do not know, or jump the

lines.speaker: GAOLER
lines.text: after-inquiry on your own peril. And how you shall speed in your

lines.speaker: GAOLER
lines.text: journey’s end, I think you’ll never return to tell one.

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: I tell thee, fellow, there are none want eyes to direct them the way I

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: am going, but such as wink and will not use them.

lines.speaker: GAOLER
lines.text: What an infinite mock is this, that a man should have the best use of

lines.speaker: GAOLER
lines.text: eyes to see the way of blindness! I am sure hanging’s the way of

lines.speaker: GAOLER
lines.text: winking.
Enter a Messenger.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Knock off his manacles; bring your prisoner to the King.

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Thou bring’st good news: I am call’d to be made free.

lines.speaker: GAOLER
lines.text: I’ll be hang’d then.

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Thou shalt be then freer than a gaoler; no bolts for the dead.
[_Exeunt Posthumus and Messenger._]

lines.speaker: GAOLER
lines.text: Unless a man would marry a gallows and beget young gibbets, I never saw

lines.speaker: GAOLER
lines.text: one so prone. Yet, on my conscience, there are verier knaves desire to

lines.speaker: GAOLER
lines.text: live, for all he be a Roman; and there be some of them too that die

lines.speaker: GAOLER
lines.text: against their wills; so should I, if I were one. I would we were all of

lines.speaker: GAOLER
lines.text: one mind, and one mind good. O, there were desolation of gaolers and

lines.speaker: GAOLER
lines.text: gallowses! I speak against my present profit, but my wish hath a

lines.speaker: GAOLER
lines.text: preferment in’t.
[_Exit._]
Enter Cymbeline, Belarius, Guiderius, Arviragus, Pisanio, Lords, Officers and Attendants.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Stand by my side, you whom the gods have made

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Preservers of my throne. Woe is my heart

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: That the poor soldier that so richly fought,

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Whose rags sham’d gilded arms, whose naked breast

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Stepp’d before targes of proof, cannot be found.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: He shall be happy that can find him, if

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Our grace can make him so.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: I never saw

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Such noble fury in so poor a thing;

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Such precious deeds in one that promis’d nought

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: But beggary and poor looks.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: No tidings of him?

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: He hath been search’d among the dead and living,

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: But no trace of him.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: To my grief, I am

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: The heir of his reward, [_To Belarius, Guiderius, and Arviragus_] which

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: I will add

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: To you, the liver, heart, and brain of Britain,

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: By whom I grant she lives. ’Tis now the time

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: To ask of whence you are. Report it.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Sir,

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: In Cambria are we born, and gentlemen;

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Further to boast were neither true nor modest,

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Unless I add we are honest.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Bow your knees.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Arise my knights o’ th’ battle; I create you

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Companions to our person, and will fit you

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: With dignities becoming your estates.
Enter Cornelius and Ladies.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: There’s business in these faces. Why so sadly

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Greet you our victory? You look like Romans,

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: And not o’ th’ court of Britain.

lines.speaker: CORNELIUS
lines.text: Hail, great King!

lines.speaker: CORNELIUS
lines.text: To sour your happiness I must report

lines.speaker: CORNELIUS
lines.text: The Queen is dead.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Who worse than a physician

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Would this report become? But I consider

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: By med’cine life may be prolong’d, yet death

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Will seize the doctor too. How ended she?

lines.speaker: CORNELIUS
lines.text: With horror, madly dying, like her life;

lines.speaker: CORNELIUS
lines.text: Which, being cruel to the world, concluded

lines.speaker: CORNELIUS
lines.text: Most cruel to herself. What she confess’d

lines.speaker: CORNELIUS
lines.text: I will report, so please you; these her women

lines.speaker: CORNELIUS
lines.text: Can trip me if I err, who with wet cheeks

lines.speaker: CORNELIUS
lines.text: Were present when she finish’d.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Prithee say.

lines.speaker: CORNELIUS
lines.text: First, she confess’d she never lov’d you; only

lines.speaker: CORNELIUS
lines.text: Affected greatness got by you, not you;

lines.speaker: CORNELIUS
lines.text: Married your royalty, was wife to your place;

lines.speaker: CORNELIUS
lines.text: Abhorr’d your person.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: She alone knew this;

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: And but she spoke it dying, I would not

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Believe her lips in opening it. Proceed.

lines.speaker: CORNELIUS
lines.text: Your daughter, whom she bore in hand to love

lines.speaker: CORNELIUS
lines.text: With such integrity, she did confess

lines.speaker: CORNELIUS
lines.text: Was as a scorpion to her sight; whose life,

lines.speaker: CORNELIUS
lines.text: But that her flight prevented it, she had

lines.speaker: CORNELIUS
lines.text: Ta’en off by poison.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: O most delicate fiend!

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Who is’t can read a woman? Is there more?

lines.speaker: CORNELIUS
lines.text: More, sir, and worse. She did confess she had

lines.speaker: CORNELIUS
lines.text: For you a mortal mineral, which, being took,

lines.speaker: CORNELIUS
lines.text: Should by the minute feed on life, and ling’ring,

lines.speaker: CORNELIUS
lines.text: By inches waste you. In which time she purpos’d,

lines.speaker: CORNELIUS
lines.text: By watching, weeping, tendance, kissing, to

lines.speaker: CORNELIUS
lines.text: O’ercome you with her show; and in time,

lines.speaker: CORNELIUS
lines.text: When she had fitted you with her craft, to work

lines.speaker: CORNELIUS
lines.text: Her son into th’ adoption of the crown;

lines.speaker: CORNELIUS
lines.text: But failing of her end by his strange absence,

lines.speaker: CORNELIUS
lines.text: Grew shameless-desperate, open’d, in despite

lines.speaker: CORNELIUS
lines.text: Of heaven and men, her purposes, repented

lines.speaker: CORNELIUS
lines.text: The evils she hatch’d were not effected; so,

lines.speaker: CORNELIUS
lines.text: Despairing, died.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Heard you all this, her women?

lines.speaker: LADIES
lines.text: We did, so please your Highness.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Mine eyes

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Were not in fault, for she was beautiful;

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Mine ears, that heard her flattery; nor my heart

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: That thought her like her seeming. It had been vicious

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: To have mistrusted her; yet, O my daughter!

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: That it was folly in me thou mayst say,

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: And prove it in thy feeling. Heaven mend all!
Enter Lucius, Iachimo, the Soothsayer and other Roman prisoners, guarded; Posthumus behind, and Imogen.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Thou com’st not, Caius, now for tribute; that

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: The Britons have raz’d out, though with the loss

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Of many a bold one, whose kinsmen have made suit

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: That their good souls may be appeas’d with slaughter

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Of you their captives, which ourself have granted;

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: So think of your estate.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Consider, sir, the chance of war. The day

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Was yours by accident; had it gone with us,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: We should not, when the blood was cool, have threaten’d

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Our prisoners with the sword. But since the gods

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Will have it thus, that nothing but our lives

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: May be call’d ransom, let it come. Sufficeth

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: A Roman with a Roman’s heart can suffer.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Augustus lives to think on’t; and so much

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: For my peculiar care. This one thing only

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: I will entreat: my boy, a Briton born,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Let him be ransom’d. Never master had

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: A page so kind, so duteous, diligent,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: So tender over his occasions, true,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: So feat, so nurse-like; let his virtue join

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: With my request, which I’ll make bold your Highness

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Cannot deny; he hath done no Briton harm

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Though he have serv’d a Roman. Save him, sir,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: And spare no blood beside.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: I have surely seen him;

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: His favour is familiar to me. Boy,

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Thou hast look’d thyself into my grace,

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: And art mine own. I know not why, wherefore

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: To say “Live, boy.” Ne’er thank thy master. Live;

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: And ask of Cymbeline what boon thou wilt,

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Fitting my bounty and thy state, I’ll give it;

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Yea, though thou do demand a prisoner,

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: The noblest ta’en.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: I humbly thank your Highness.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: I do not bid thee beg my life, good lad,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: And yet I know thou wilt.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: No, no! Alack,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: There’s other work in hand. I see a thing

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Bitter to me as death; your life, good master,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Must shuffle for itself.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: The boy disdains me,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: He leaves me, scorns me. Briefly die their joys

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: That place them on the truth of girls and boys.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Why stands he so perplex’d?

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: What wouldst thou, boy?

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: I love thee more and more; think more and more

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: What’s best to ask. Know’st him thou look’st on? Speak,

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Wilt have him live? Is he thy kin? thy friend?

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: He is a Roman, no more kin to me

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Than I to your Highness; who, being born your vassal,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Am something nearer.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Wherefore ey’st him so?

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: I’ll tell you, sir, in private, if you please

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: To give me hearing.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Ay, with all my heart,

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: And lend my best attention. What’s thy name?

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Fidele, sir.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Thou’rt my good youth, my page;

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: I’ll be thy master. Walk with me; speak freely.
[_Cymbeline and Imogen converse apart._]

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Is not this boy reviv’d from death?

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: One sand another

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: Not more resembles that sweet rosy lad

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: Who died and was Fidele. What think you?

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: The same dead thing alive.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Peace, peace! see further. He eyes us not; forbear.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Creatures may be alike; were’t he, I am sure

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: He would have spoke to us.

lines.speaker: GUIDERIUS
lines.text: But we see him dead.

lines.speaker: BELARIUS
lines.text: Be silent; let’s see further.
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: It is my mistress.

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: Since she is living, let the time run on

lines.speaker: PISANIO
lines.text: To good or bad.
[_Cymbeline and Imogen advance._]

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Come, stand thou by our side;

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Make thy demand aloud. [_To Iachimo._] Sir, step you forth;

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Give answer to this boy, and do it freely,

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Or, by our greatness and the grace of it,

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Which is our honour, bitter torture shall

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Winnow the truth from falsehood. On, speak to him.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: My boon is that this gentleman may render

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: Of whom he had this ring.
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: What’s that to him?

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: That diamond upon your finger, say

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: How came it yours?

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Thou’lt torture me to leave unspoken that

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Which to be spoke would torture thee.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: How? me?

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: I am glad to be constrain’d to utter that

lines.speaker: IACHIMO

lines.text: Is severally in all. Let’s quit this ground,

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: And smoke the temple with our sacrifices.
[_To Belarius._]

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Thou art my brother; so we’ll hold thee ever.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: You are my father too, and did relieve me

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: To see this gracious season.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: All o’erjoy’d

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Save these in bonds. Let them be joyful too,

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: For they shall taste our comfort.

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: My good master,

lines.speaker: IMOGEN
lines.text: I will yet do you service.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Happy be you!

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: The forlorn soldier, that so nobly fought,

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: He would have well becom’d this place and grac’d

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: The thankings of a king.

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: I am, sir,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: The soldier that did company these three

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: In poor beseeming; ’twas a fitment for

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: The purpose I then follow’d. That I was he,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Speak, Iachimo. I had you down, and might

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Have made you finish.
[_Kneeling._]

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: I am down again;

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: But now my heavy conscience sinks my knee,

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: As then your force did. Take that life, beseech you,

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: Which I so often owe; but your ring first,

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: And here the bracelet of the truest princess

lines.speaker: IACHIMO
lines.text: That ever swore her faith.

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Kneel not to me.

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: The pow’r that I have on you is to spare you;

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: The malice towards you to forgive you. Live,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: And deal with others better.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Nobly doom’d!

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: We’ll learn our freeness of a son-in-law;

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Pardon’s the word to all.

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: You holp us, sir,

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: As you did mean indeed to be our brother;

lines.speaker: ARVIRAGUS
lines.text: Joy’d are we that you are.

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Your servant, Princes. Good my lord of Rome,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Call forth your soothsayer. As I slept, methought

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Great Jupiter, upon his eagle back’d,

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Appear’d to me, with other spritely shows

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Of mine own kindred. When I wak’d, I found

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: This label on my bosom; whose containing

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Is so from sense in hardness that I can

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: Make no collection of it. Let him show

lines.speaker: POSTHUMUS
lines.text: His skill in the construction.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Philarmonus!

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: Here, my good lord.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Read, and declare the meaning.
[_Reads._]

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: _When as a lion’s whelp shall, to himself unknown, without

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: seeking find, and be embrac’d by a piece of tender air; and when from a

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: stately cedar shall be lopp’d branches which, being dead many years,

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: shall after revive, be jointed to the old stock, and freshly grow; then

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: shall Posthumus end his miseries, Britain be fortunate and flourish in

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: peace and plenty._

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: Thou, Leonatus, art the lion’s whelp;

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: The fit and apt construction of thy name,

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: Being Leo-natus, doth import so much.
[_To Cymbeline_]

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: The piece of tender air, thy virtuous daughter,

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: Which we call _mollis aer_, and _mollis aer_

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: We term it _mulier_; which _mulier_ I divine

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: Is this most constant wife, who even now

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: Answering the letter of the oracle,

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: Unknown to you, unsought, were clipp’d about

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: With this most tender air.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: This hath some seeming.

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: The lofty cedar, royal Cymbeline,

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: Personates thee; and thy lopp’d branches point

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: Thy two sons forth, who, by Belarius stol’n,

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: For many years thought dead, are now reviv’d,

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: To the majestic cedar join’d, whose issue

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: Promises Britain peace and plenty.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Well,

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: My peace we will begin. And, Caius Lucius,

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Although the victor, we submit to Cæsar

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: And to the Roman empire, promising

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: To pay our wonted tribute, from the which

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: We were dissuaded by our wicked queen,

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Whom heavens in justice, both on her and hers,

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Have laid most heavy hand.

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: The fingers of the pow’rs above do tune

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: The harmony of this peace. The vision

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: Which I made known to Lucius ere the stroke

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: Of yet this scarce-cold battle, at this instant

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: Is full accomplish’d; for the Roman eagle,

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: From south to west on wing soaring aloft,

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: Lessen’d herself and in the beams o’ th’ sun

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: So vanish’d; which foreshow’d our princely eagle,

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: Th’ imperial Cæsar, should again unite

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: His favour with the radiant Cymbeline,

lines.speaker: SOOTHSAYER
lines.text: Which shines here in the west.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Laud we the gods;

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: And let our crooked smokes climb to their nostrils

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: From our bless’d altars. Publish we this peace

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: To all our subjects. Set we forward; let

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: A Roman and a British ensign wave

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Friendly together. So through Lud’s Town march;

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: And in the temple of great Jupiter

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Our peace we’ll ratify; seal it with feasts.

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Set on there! Never was a war did cease,

lines.speaker: CYMBELINE
lines.text: Ere bloody hands were wash’d, with such a peace.
[_Exeunt._]
